Sub; Disposal of grievances under EPFIGMS — Performance Review -
regarding.

Sir/ Madam,

On Review of disposal of cases under EPFIGMS it has emerged that only
67 ROs/SROs have receipt of grievances averaging to one or more per day,
Remaining offices have receipt less than one per day.

Clearly it is expected that the offices having receipt of less than one per
day shall be disposing off all gnevances without accumulating any
pendency and shall have nil closing balance of grievances as on 31™*
March, 2015.

For offices having receipts of one Of more also it is expected that the
disposal must be more tan receipts so that no further pendency is
accumulated. However, on Review of the performance of such ROs/SROs (list
enclosed) it is seen that an aeath day of the year only 28 ROs/SROs have
disposed off grievances more than receipts, whereas 93 ROs/SROs have
disposed off grievances Equivalent to the receipt.

It is a cause of great concern that 36 ROs/SROs have disposed off
grievances less than the receipts. Accordingly, all such Ros/SROs shall
immediately Review the pending grievances so as to ensure that they achieve
4 disposal of more than receipts during the year,

All offices having pendency as on 31" March, 2015 having
disposed off grievances less than receipts during the year shall submit
reason for accumulating pendency ina single page note signed by OIC
by 08" April, 2015 to the ACC (Political States). The ACC shall examine
the reasons and submit a single page note covering all such offices
under his jurisdiction to Head Office by 16" April, 2015.

Further, it is seen that still 45 ROs/SROs have grievances Pending for
more than 15 days (list enclosed). For all such cases the OIC shall be
responsible to Review the individual cases and submit a report to Acc
(Political States) by 10% April, 2015, case wise clearly giving the
reason for the grievance remaining Pending for more than 15 days.
The ACC (Political States) shall forward 4 consolidated report for all
Such offices under his jurisdiction to Head Office by 20" April, 2015.
Where the grievance has remained Pending on account of the
grievance having pertained to some other RO/SRO, the copy of letter
written to the other RO/SRO along with details of telephonic calls
made to the OIC of the other RO/SRO must be furnished so that the
same be placed before CPFC.

Further, it is also informed that it fs expected that the disposals are done
to the satisfaction of the complainant and the quality of disposal is maintained.
The quality of disposal done by individual RO/SPO is also being reviewed
seperately, The result of the FeVIEW shall be intimated next month to- all
concerned.

Yours faithfully,

Sir,
The performance
of Field Offices in the area of recovery of Current Demand (CD) and Arrear
Demand (AD) during Special Recovery Drive for the month of February,
2015 has been reviewed.
2.
Recovery
of Current
Demand (Un-Exemnted):
G)
As per the instructions
contained
in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012 (placed in the Official
Website of the Organization
at SI No. 187/2012). The targets set in the area of recovery of Current
Demand is 100%. It is observed that during Special Recovery Drive for the month of February, 2015,
all Regions failed to achieve
the target. Only Ahmedabad, Baroda, Ludhiana , Ranchi and Bangalore
Regions have made recovery above 30% whereas rest of the Regions have
performed poorly as the
recovery made during this Special Recovery Drive is less than 3% .
Recovery
of Current

(ii)

the target of 100% recovery
which is well appreciated whereas the performance of rest of the Regions is found not satisfactory.
Recovery
of Arrear
Demand (Un-Exempted
& Exempted):
(iii)
As per the instructions
contained
in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012 (placed in the Official
Website of the Organization
at SI No. 187/2012), the targets set in the area of recovery. of Arrear
Demand is 80%. It is observed that performance of all Regions in the area of Arrear Demand (both in

area shows ineffectiveness
and poor monitoring in handling Compliance Machinery. All the ACCs of

of fixed targets.

Quarters.

Sub: Construction projects at various EPFO offices and other miscellaneous works to the

executed by CPWD - regarding.
Sir,

As you are aware that for new construction projects as well as special repairs at various

offices the works has been/is to be allotted to CPWD from time to time.

In this regard a number of references are being received from various offices from which

it appears that there is a need to clarify the following points:

1. Scope of work for new construction projects:

For all new construction projects the scope of works shall be strictly as per estimates
approved by the Executive Committee, CBT and no change to the approved scope of
works shall be made by any ACC/RPFC subsequently except for minor changes within a
head/subhead having no financial implication. Furtner, offices who are yet to submit a
proposal for a new construction project must ensure that the proposal of the layout be
strictly in accordance with the SIU Norms, the observations of Building & Construction, Sub
Committee and the austerity measures in force. For example in SROs Guest House must
not be proposed unless there be a very very strong and compelling reasons to do so.
Similarly, it is seen that few offices have provided for unnecessary work items like rest
room for OIC, library etc. such proposals may please not be sent as it unnecessarily delays

the approval of conceptual plans.

rh

SS

2. Getting approval from local authorities. :

Once the scope of work and estimates is approved by Executive Committee the ACC and
the RPFC concerned must ensure that the approval of local authority is immediately
obtained in consultation with CPWD. The ACC/RPFC must use their good offices to
obtain necessary approval at the earliest.

3. Initial deposit:

The issue of initial deposit was taken up with CPWD and accordingly for miscellaneous
works of technical_nature like installation of transformers, lifts etc. initial deposit of 30%
may be released as per demand of CPWD in specific cases if need be even 100%
advance may be given subject to approval of Head Office. However, for construction
projects the initial deposit shall be 10% plus 10% as per the proposed agreement
between CPWD & EPFO which shall be based upon the agreement between ESIC and
CPWD (copy enclosed). The budget provision has been made in the RE 2014-15 and BE
2015-16. The demand of 20% budget of approved estimated cost may be placed before
Finance Division, Head Office directly and same is to be released as per terms and
conditions of the agreement as finalized between ESIC and CPWD after execution of
agreement between EPFO & CPWD.

Agency charges:

The agency charges are presently under negotiation between EPFO & CPWD and are
likely to be 50% of standard departmental charges as per CPWD work manual.

Leaving scope for further expansion:

lt has been seen that earlier the various offices were leaving scope for vertical expansion
which later on is creating a number of difficulties at the time of actual expansion.
Accordingly, it is requested that while preparing and forwarding any conceptual plan for
construction of office/residential complex the scope may be left for horizontal expansion
by utilizing the permissible vertical height for the proposed new building.

Fire Fighting System in Office Building:

Provision of fire fighting system in office buildings should be strictly as per provisions of
National Building Code - 2005 and local bylaws.

(This issue with the approval of Central P.F. Commissioner)

Sub: Review of Suspension
Sir,

Please refer to circulars dated 21.11.2005 and 25.11.2005 issued by
the Vigilance Wing in the matter of review of suspension.

2. As per CCS (CCA} Rules 1965, an order of suspension made or
deemed to have been made under the said Rule shall be reviewed by the
authority competent to modify or revoke suspension, before expiry of 90
days from the date of order of suspension and thet extension of suspension
shall not be for a period exceeding 180 days at a time. However, it is seen
that many a time there is a delay in the decision of the Disciplinary
Authority regarding review of suspension. Protracted and repeated
correspondence with Head Office is sometimes responsible for the delay.
Delay in review means automatic revocation of suspension, which when
unintended is a series matter.

3. I am directed to request to all the R.P.F.Cs; OICs of the ROs/ SROs
to ensure that mandatory reviews of suspension cases are carried out
without exception as any such failure may render a suspension technically
wrong as the suspension is continued without the mandatory review. Even
in cases where the RO/ SRO has referred the matter to Head Office, the
Review Committee should necessarily carry out the review even in the event
of non-receipt of Head Office recommendation. In such cases the decision
taken may be informed to Head office with the copy of Review Committee’s
Recommendations.

4. Strict compliance of the above directions may please be ensured.

Yours faithfully

In the matter of - Mandatory filing of return in Form-5A online by the employers of the
establishments covered under the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 (the Act).

1. Paragraph 36-A of the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 stipulates that every employer in
relation to a factory or other establishment to which the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952(the Act) applies, shall furnish in duplicate to the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner a
retum on particulars of ownership in Form 5A showing the particulars of all the branches and departments
owners, occupiers, directors, partners, manager or any other person or persons who have the ultimate control
over the affairs of such factory or establishment.

2. Till date, the employers of the establishments covered under the Act were submitting ownership returns
in Form 5A manually. However when the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation has embarked upon its next
phase of e-governance reforms with a view to make its services available to its stakeholders in an efficient,
transparent and reliable manner and at low costs, it becomes imperative that the establishments furnish
statutory returns electronically.

3, Sub-Paragraph 7 of Paragraph 36 of the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 states as under :

(7) Every employer shall send to the Commissioner such returns in electronic format also, in
such form and manner as may be specified by the Commissioner.

4. Now, in exercise of powers conferred by the above paragraph of Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme,
1952, it is directed that employers of establishments covered under the Employees’ Provident Funds &
Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 shall mandatorily file Form 5A online with the Employees’ Provident Fund
Organisation w.e.f. 25% February, 2015 that is from the date of issue of this order.

5. The establishments which have already submitted the return in Form 5A manually are also directed to
file the said return online.

6. It is also mandated that the deadline for filing of return in Form 5A is fixed as 318t March,2015.Failure to
file the said return online by 31st March,2015 will amount to non-submission of statutory return and also render
the defaulting establishment liable for action as provided under Section 14 of the Act.

Subject:- | Procedure for Cancellation of Exemption - Regarding.
Sir,

Section 17(1)(a) and 17(2) of the EPF & MP Act, 1952 provides for grant of exemption to the applicant
establishments from the operation of the provisions of the EPF Scheme, 1952 and Section 17(4) of the Act
provides for cancellation of exemption.

2. Head Office has issued guidelines vide Circular No. Exem/6(20)08/DL/NZ/Vol.| /30327 Dated:
30.07.2009(copy thereof enclosed for ready reference) regarding procedure to be followed by the field offices
while processing cases relating to cancellation/surrender of exemption.

3. In recent communications, Ministry of Labour & Employment has instructed that audited accounts of the
Trust of the exempted establishment and an assessment whether any liability is likely to arise on EPFO as a
result of the rate of interest announced by EPFO being also admissible to these subscribers, is also required to
be submitted.

4, Therefore, it is instructed that in future while forwarding the proposals for cancellation/surrender of
exemption of the establishments, the above said requirement be fulfilled invariably by the RPFCs as a standard
procedure in all such cases so that there is no cross subsidization by other subscribers. In case any liability
arises, it may also be indicated how RPFC proposes to deal with if.

5. It is also instructed to get the fund audited and ascertain the financial health of the Trust by a third party
auditor in accordance with the instructions contained in Head Office circular No. E-II/Misc./14/Exem/Third Party
Compliance Audit/2682 dated 30.04.2012 in all such cases in future.

6. It is further instructed wherever any proposal for cancellation/surrender of exemption is pending at any
level, this exercise be got completed and a report be furnished to the Head Office urgently.

Subject : Proposals for voluntary coverage under Section 1(4) of Employees’ Provident Funds

& Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952.
Section 1(4) of the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (the Act) provides:

“Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section(3) of this section or sub-section (1) of Section 16,
where it appears to the Central Provident Fund Commissioner, whether on an application made fo him in this
behalf or otherwise, that the employer and majority of employees in relation to any establishment have agreed
that the provisions of this Act should be made applicable to the establishment, he may, by notification in the
Official Gazette, apply the provisions of this Act to that establishment on and from the date of such agreement or
from any subsequent date specified in such agreement.”

2. You are aware that the establishments which are not coverable either under Section 1(3)(a) or Section
1(3)(b) of the Act, can apply for coverage under Section 1(4) of the Act. Coverage made under Section 1(4) of the
Act are considered as voluntary coverage. In all cases of establishments so covered under Section 1(4) of the Act

notification is required to be issued for application of the Act to the establishment by the Central Provident Fund
Commissioner in the Official Gazette.

3. As per existing instructions issued from Head office, after issue of code number under Section 1(4) of the
Act, Regional/Sub-Regional Offices are required to send proposal to Head Office through the Additional Central
PF Commissioner (Zones) for approval of Centra! Provident Fund Commissioner. Once the proposal is approved
by Central Provident Fund Commissioner, necessary approval is conveyed to Additional Central PF
Commissioner (Zones) for arranging notification in the Official Gazette at their level.

4, This has not been done in all cases of Section 1(4) coverage. In the Internal Audit and the AG (Central)
Audit observed that in majority of cases proposals have not been forwarded by Regional/Sub-Regional Offices to
Head Office through Additional CPFC (Zones) for approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner and issue of
notification. This has been adversely commented by C&AG of India.

In the instant matter,
Hon'ble
Supreme Court ofIndia
has held that when damages u/s14B of the EPF&MP
Act are imposed
upon any employer,
then the successor
employer
to
whom the establishment
in question is transferred
CAN NOT escape from his liability imposed
u/s-17B of the Act by giving the following excuses:-
(i)
that
the penalty,
u/s-14B
has criminal
character
and therefore
can't
be transferred
to the
successor.
(ii)
that the ratio of Supreme
Court judgement
in the case of ESIC
Vs. HMT
(2008)
saves the
successor
from the liability
u/s-14B
by virtue of the principle
of "mens
rea" i.e. because
the
successor
was not the "employer"
at the time of default.
(iii)
that Section
17B talks only of contributions
& other sums and does not include
14 damages.
3.
The Apex
Court further
held that unlike
Section
7A, amount
need not be determined
under
section
17B for the purposes
of recovery
u/s-14B.
4.
The
Hon'ble
Court
also
held
that
section
7A(2) would
also
be available
to
proceedings
Under Section 14B of the Act.
The applicability
code of Civil Procedure,
1908 to
proceedings Under Section 14B has not specifically been barred by the statute".

5.
Therefore,
this landmark
order of Hon'ble
High Court may be utilised
not only in recovering
the 14B damages
but also in defending
the court cases related to recovery
of 14B damages
from the
successor
employer
u/s-17B
of the Act.
Yours faithfully

action for defending the case.

monthly basis by Zonal ACCs and during Enforcement Officers meeting. Development be
closely monitored.

be especially reviewed by ZonalAdd]. Central P.F Commissioners/Regional Provident Fund

Subject:- Constitution of Review Committees for the purpose of reviewing suspension of
suspended cases on administrative ground cases-regarding.
Sir,
Please refer to Head Office letter No. HRD/P-IV/2(6)84/CCA/Vol.II/31368 dated
13.07.2005 whereby a Notification on EPF Staff (CCA) Rules, 2005 as published in the Gazette
of India on 04.06.2005 was forwarded for information and necessary action.

2. As per aforesaid notification, a new rule i.e. Rule 28 has been inserted in the EPF Staff
(CCA) Rules, 1971, which is reproduced as under:

“28 Saving Clause:

Government of India/Department of Personnel & Training’s instructions/Clarifications,
issued from time to time with regard to CCS (CC&A) Rules, 1965 shall also apply to the
employees of Central Board mutatis mutandis so far as these relate to and are not inconsistent
with any of the provisions of EPF Staff (CCA) Rules, 1971.”

3. Govt. of India (DOP & T) had notified an amendment to Rule 10 of CCS (CC8&A)
Rules, 1965 vide Notification dated 23 December 2003. By way of this amendment, an
order of suspension made or deemed to have been made under the said Rule shall be
reviewed by the authority competent to modify or revoke suspension, before expiry of 90
days from the date of order of suspension and that extension of suspension shall not be
for a period exceeding 180 days at a time. The same shall be done on the
recommendation of the Review Committee constituted for this purpose and pas orders
either extending or revoking the suspension. Separately vide O.M. No. 11012/4/2003Estt. (A) dated 7" January 2004, guidelines have been prescribed for the composition of
Review Committee which shall take a view regarding the fact whether an official under
suspension shall continue to be so or the order so suspension needs to be revoked and
the competent authority shall take further action on the basis of such recommendation.

4. It is also relevant to mention that as per Rule 6 of the EPF Staff (CC&A) Rules, 1971, the
particular set of Rules applicable to the employees of Central Board of Trustees, an
order of suspension continues to be in force till it is modified or revoked by the

Letters in- Det, 2014

competent authority. The requirement of mandatory periodical reviews is not provided fro
in the same in the manner envisaged by DOP&T. However, the suspension of the
officials in EPFO was being reviewed from time to time by the competent authority in

5. Consequent of insertion of Rule 28 (as reproduced at Para 2 above) which provided that
the instructions of DO&T shall apply with equal force to the EPF Staff (CC&A) Rules,
1971, the constitution of Review Committees for various levels of officials/officers placed

dated pt November,
1990,
amending
para 26(2)
of EPF scheme
as under:
"After
this paragraph
come into force, in a factory
or other
establishment,
every
employee
employed
in
or
in
connection
with
the
work
of
that
factory
or
establishment
other
than excluded employee
who has not become a member
already
shall be entitled
and required
to become
a member
of the fund
from
the date of
joining
the factory or establishment.
11
2.
The
validity
of
para
26(2)
of the
scheme
was
upheld
by the
Hon'ble
Supreme
Court in J.P. Tobacco
Products.
Hon'ble Apex court held that the amendment
to para 26(2)
of the scheme
was valid and compulsory
contribution
towards
Provident
Fund does not amount
to denial of minimum
wages.
Hon'ble Apex Court
further
held
that the amendment
is not impracticable
and unworkable;
is not ultra-vires
to the Act
and Article
14 and 19(1)
(g) of the constitution
of India.
The petitioner
in the case
mentioned
in subject
had also filed a writ petition
under Article
32 before the Supreme
Court
which
was
clubbed
with
the
J.P. Tobacco
case
and
therefore
are
bound
to
comply
with the orders
of Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the matter
of
J.P. Tobacco.
3.
A civil
writ
petition
titled
Pvare
Lal Hari
Singh
Vs Union
of India
and
others
WP ( C ) No. 792/1991
was also filed before Delhi High Court wherein
the vires
of para 26(2)
of the Scheme
were challenged
with
regard
to
contribution
to be made
related
to
the
migrant
labourers
going
from
place
to
place.
Though
the
Hon'ble
Division
Bench passed various
orders from
time
to time
on the
measures
to be taken
by
the
respondents,
but at
no occasion,
the Hon'ble court said that the
validity of para 26{ 2) is ultra vires.

4.
However
the Hon'ble
Delhi High Court,
in its various
orders also directed
for formulation
of proper and effective
Scheme so that the benefits
can be extended
to
the casual/migrant/peripatetic
workers
in a hassle free manner.
5.
On May 02, 1995, the judgment
of Hon'ble Supreme
Court in J.P. Tobacco
case on para
26(2)
of the
Scheme
was
brought
to
the
notice
of Hon'ble
Division
Bench.
It was argued
by the
counsel
of the
petitioners
that
the
Hon'ble
Supreme
Court
considered
only
four
points
in the
SLPs which
were
against
the judgment
of
Hon'ble
Madhya
Pradesh
High Court
and there
is a fifth
ground
which
is yet
to be
considered
which is
:
"If
a casual workers for a very brief period works in an establishment
will he
be covered
under
the definition
of
Employee"
under
the EPF & MP Act, 1952." The
Division Bench in view of the decision of the Supreme Court
vacated the interim
order
granted
earlier
and directed
that
the respondent
number
1 and 2
complying
with
modified
scheme the petitioner
shall deduct the Provident
Fund and deposit the same
with respondent
number 1 & 2 in respect of
casual workers also. "
6.
The said writ
petitions
filed
by M/s Builders
Association
of India
& Ors.
were finally
disposed of by Hon'ble High Court vide order dated 28-08-2014
observing
that
in view of the fact that
the vires of the amended
para 26(2)
has been upheld by
the
Supreme
Court,
the
prayer
made
in this
writ
petition
for
a direction
not to
enforce
the
provision
of amended
para 26(2)
of the
scheme
is totally
misconceived
and
unsustainable
Accordingly,
the
writ
petition
no. WP ( C ) 9500/2009
was
dismissed.
7.
As regards
the WP (C)
Nos. 3588/2002,
7253/2002,
8956-57/2005
&
1213/2006,
the
Hon'ble
court
in
its
order
dated
28-08-2014
observed
that
the
petitioners
were
under
obligation
to
give
the
requisite
informations
/cornplete
records/details
with
regard to casual labourers
as directed,
surely to ensure
that the
petitioners
discharge
their
obligation
under the Scheme
without
delay.
From a legal
perspective,
it has to
be said that
a statutory
provision
cannot
be nullified
on the
ground of procedural
deficiency,
if any.
Hon'ble
High Court observed
that
denial of such facility
(to withdraw
the
amount
from
any
place
of
his
convenience)
cannot
be
a
grievance
of
the
employer/petitioner
the objective
of the Acts/Scheme
can't
be defeated
only on
the
ground
that
the facility
of withdrawing
the
money
has not been evolved.
The
stand
of
petitioners
that
till
PAN number
is allotted,
they
are
unable
to
deposit
contribution,
is unsustainable.
The amount
of Rs. 26000
crores
lying
in inoperative
account
cannot
be a ground
for the petitioners
to make
a provision
of the Scheme
unworkable.
The Hon'ble High Court expressed that the respondents
must put in place a
Scheme which would facilitate
the withdrawal
of money
by a peripatetic
worker
from
any place in the country,
at the earliest,
if not done till date.
The Hon'ble
High Court allowed
the action
initiated
by the respondents
to
continue
in accordance
with law.
The writ petitions
were dismissed.

unit, clinical and pathological laboratory fall within the meaning
of Hospital-Regarding.

Sir,

Please find enclosed herewith a copy of the judgement delivered by
Hon’ble High Court of Kerala in Writ Appeal No. 1225/2009 dated 18.11.2014
(copy enclosed).

2 The Hon’ble High Court of Kerala has disposed the Writ Appeal No.
1225/2009 filed by M/s Kottayam District Hospital Society Ltd against the
judgement in OP No. 14067/2002 vide its Judgement dated 18.11.2014. The
Hon’ble court has further held that:

(a) a Co-operative society registered under the Kerala Co-operative
Societies Act is not created by the said Act and therefore cannot be
said to be set up under a state Act as envisaged in section 16(1)( C)
of the EPF Act, 1952.

(b) and that the establishment which is a CAT/CT scan unit, a clinical
and pathological laboratory falls within the meaning of Hospitals and
are coverable under section 1(3)(b) of the EPF & MP Act, 1952.

3 Therefore, this landmark Judgement of Hon‘ble High Court may be
utilised in defending similar cases.

Subject: Performance Review regarding recovery of Current Demand & Arrear Demand for the
month of October, 2014, November, 2014 — reg.

Sir,

The performance of Field Offices in the area of recovery of Current Demand (CD) and Arrear
Demand {AD) for the month of October, 2014, November, 2014 has been reviewed.

2. Recovery of Current Demand:

(a) As per the instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012 (placed in the Official
Website of the Organization at SI No. 187/2012). The targets set in the area of recovery of Current
Demand in Immediately Realizable Category is 100%. it is observed from the performance of all regions
for the month October, 2014 that Regional Offices. Bangalore, Jaipur, Baroda, Ahmedabad and Ranchi,
have achieved the recovery to the tune of more than 80% which is weil appreciated. During November,
2014 Regional Offices, Ahmedabad, Bangalore & Jaipur performed excellently as the recovery is more
than 85%.

(b) Wheres the performance of Regional office, Bhubaneshwar .Kanpur, Kandivili &Patna is very poor in
the area of Current Demand (Immediately Realizable Category) is very poor as the recovery is less than
26% during the month of October, 2014. In the month of November, 2014, Regional Offices,
Bhubaneshwar, Kanpur& kandivili performed poorly. It is observed that during both months,
Bhubaneshwar Region has made recovery less than 3% which is a matter of great concern. ACC(Zone) is
requested to look into the matter personally.

Recovery of Arrear Demand:

(c) As per the instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012 (placed in the Official
Website of the Organization at Si No. 187/2012). The targets set in the area of recovery of Arrear
Demand in Immediately Realizable Category is 80%. It is observed that performance of all regions in the
area of Arrear Demand in Immediately Realizable Category (IR) during October & November, 2014 is
not upto the mark, Only Baroda, Delhi(North}) and Kolkata Regions have made recovery above 60%.
Low percentage of recovery in the above area shows ineffectiveness and poor monitoring in handling
Compliance Machinery. All the ACCs of the Zones are requested to bestow their persona? attention and
take necessary steps to ensure achieving of targets

3. In view of the above, All ACCs are requested to direct all RPFCs/OICs under their jurisdiction to
make Action Plan for recovery of Current Demand & Arrear Demand and deploy suitable officers/officiats so as
to ensure that the fixed targets are achieved within time limit.

Yours faithfully

Addl. Central P.F. Commissioner (Recovery)

SOCIAL SECURITY AGREEMENT WITH THE KINGDOM OF NORWAY

The Government of India has entered into an Agreement on Social
Security Agreement with the kingdom of Norway. Following the principles of
reciprocity this agreement is intended to benefit the employees of both India as
well as the Kingdom of Norway. The agreement has come into force w.e.f. 1°!
January, 2015.

The Agreement provides, inter-alta, for posting i.e. detachment up to a
period of 60 months for employees of both the countries. Accordingly, the
employees of one country deputed by their employers to the other country on
short-term assignment for a pre-determined period of up to a period of 60
months need not remit Social Security contributions in that country. Thus, the
employers are saved from making double Social Security contributions for the
same set of employees thereby enhancing the competitiveness of their products
and services.

Employees’ Provident Fund Organization (EPFO) has been identified as
the agency to implement the provisions of the agreement in India and has been
authorized to issue “Certificate of coverage” to the employees of Indian
establishments posted to the Kingdom of Norway.

Therefore, the employers who have already deputed/intend to depute
their employees to the Kingdom of Norway can avail of this facility. The
application form for this purpose is available on the official website
http:/Awww.epfindia.gov.in/ under the tab "International worker’.The “Certificate
of coverage” will be issued by concerned RO/SRO where the application is
submitted. They may also contact their jurisdictional Regional Provident Fund
Commissioner or the International Workers Unit in the Head Office at 14, Bhikaiji
Cama Place, New Delhi- 110066 for any further details.

Sub:- Issues regarding Shram Suvidha Porta! and other Inspections raised
by the Regional Office, Chennai during the review on 31.12.2014 —
regarding.

Sir,

During the review of the Tamil Nadu and Kerala Regions by the
CPFC on 31.12.2014, few issues related to the Inspections and the Shram
Suvidha Portal were raised by the Regional Office, Chennai. The issues
have been analysed and the status on these issues is as under:-

1. Training of the Inspectors for the use of Shram Suvidha Portal:
Initially training of the Master Trainers was done at NATRSS and
the trainers were to train the others. Also the User Manual was
sent to all the Officers and SMS alert was also sent for checking the

“mail. Thereafter a few changes have been made on the Portal for
facilitating the smooth submission of the Reports by the
Enforcement Officers. An updated User Manual is being called from
the NIC Team that has developed the Portal and will be sent to all

Subject : Coverage of construction and contract workers under the ambit of the Employees’
Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 - Regarding.

The issue of coverage of construction and contract workers under the ambit of the Employees’
Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 has been a matter of concern for Employees’
Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). A number of instructions were issued in past on the subject.

2. It has been the presumption of field offices of EPFO that the workers engaged by the establishments
carrying out business in ‘Building & Construction Industry’ are construction workers and workers engaged by
establishments rendering “Expert Services” are contract workers. EPFO has been struggling to cover all eligible
workers engaged in these two classes of establishments. !t may so happen that establishments covered under
other schedule heads and class of establishments might be deploying construction and contract workers for
various purposes. Somehow, all eligible workers are not enrolled as PF members.

3. In this regard, your attention is drawn to this office circular No. C11/410001/4/3(71)MISC /2013/DL/12882 dated 08.10.2013 (attached as Annexure-3A) wherein you were
advised to start a dialogue with the Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous Bodies and
apprise their responsibilities as Principal Employers while engaging personnel for watch-ward, house-keeping,
data entry etc. through various agencies and contractors. You were also advised to ask other establishments
deploying more than 500 workers to enroll all eligible workers deployed by or through contractors engaged by
them. You were also advised to see that :

a) All the agencies and contractors to whom the work is outsourced are covered under the Act;
b) All the personnel supplied by the agencies and contractors are extended benefits of provident fund etc.;
and

c) All the personnel engaged get eligible benefits commensurate to the wage they get.

5. During the meeting of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Labour held on 28.10.2014, Hon'ble
Members raised their concern on the gaps in the coverage of construction and contract workers under the
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 and accordingly, instructions were issued
vide this office letters dated 05.11.2014 (attached herewith as Annexure ~ 5A and Annexure - 5B) to launch a
campaign from 15.11.2014 to 15.01.2015 to enroll all eligible construction and contract workers.

Page 1 of 2

6. The Parliamentary Standing Committee on Labour in their last meeting held on 01.01.2015 at Tirupati
desired that EPFO should work hard on coverage of construction and contract workers.

7. In that backdrop, the Central PF Commissioner has issued following instructions through e-mail on
08.01.2015 to all of you :

a) Meetings of Railways and other Central Government authorities/departments be held by you
regarding coverage of contract and construction workers. Proceedings of the same be drawn
up and action taken on the same.

b) A meeting of all the State PSUs and State Departments be also called wherever it is felt that
the workers are taken on outsource. They should also be apprised of the EPF & MP Act,
1952. The proceedings of the same may also be drawn up and action taken on the same.

c) As earlier ordered vide circular No.C-III/110001/4/3(71)Misc./2013/DL/12802 dated 8 October,
2013, all the establishments which are having 500 plus employees shall be visited and the
date-wise information regarding visit to the same may be sent.

d) The meetings be called of all the establishments which have 100 plus employees, may be in
batches, and all companies should be asked to comply with the provisions. Meetings of ail the
builders and developers in the area should be called and proceedings of the same be drawn
and action taken.

e) At least 5 to 10 meetings be conducted in the areas where labourers are predominantly
residing (involving Labour Unions also). The details of these should also be brought to the
notice of the Headquarters.

8. In view of above, all the Regional PF Commissioners, In-Charge of Regional and Sub-Regional Offices
are directed to ensure that all eligible workers working in all the establishments engaged in Building &
Construction industry and the workers working with different establishments by or through contractors are
enrolled. The information on such enrolment of construction and contract workers may be sent to Head Office in
the format already prescribed.

Sub: Achievement of target given in Annual Plan 2014-15 in respect of

Sir

As you are aware that as per the target given in Annual Plan there shall
be of total pendency of not more than 10% for cases pending for more than
15 days.

However, it is seen that as on today out of total 4695 pending cases as
many as 1236 no. of cases are pending for more than 15 days which makes

pending case. The detailed pendency list is enclosed herewith. As may be
seen highest pendency is in Regional Office, Bandra for which the concerned
RPFC-I shall be required to reduce the pendency as much as possible.

However, in order to keep the margin for offices like Bandra who may
not be able to attain the target of having only 10% cases of pending for more
than 15 days, it is necessary that other offices ensure and strive for attaining
a nil pendency or of not more than 5% of cases pending for more than 15

Subject : Organising awareness camps for workers - Regarding.

Sir,

A number of initiatives have been taken by Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation in the interest of
employees working in the establishments covered under the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952 (the Act).

2. The details of the initiatives taken in the interest of PF members are as under :

a) Digitization of complete database of EPF subscribers and allotment of Universal Account
Number (UAN) to each of them for portability of their accounts on change of job or location.

b) Seeding of UAN with bank account, Aadhar Card and other KYC details for financial inclusion.

c) For members EPFO claim forms can be accessed from the EPF India website:
htto://epf.india..gov.in/downloads forms.htm

d) By registering on EPFO portal, members can access PF accounts online with real-time updates.
Members can view and print account statements multiple times without any employer intervention.
Members will receive an SMS alert each time the PF account has been credited or debited.

e) Statutory wage ceiling enhanced to Rs. 15,000 w.e.f. 01.09.2014.

f) For the first time, a minimum pension of Rs. 1000/- per month has been introduced w.e-f.
01.09.2014 for 2014-15.

g) Employees' Pension Scheme is a scheme where widows and children are benefited. The widows
of deceased PF members would be entitled to a lifelong widow pension. Similarly the children of
deceased PF members would be entitled to a pension up to the age of 25. The pension is
admissible for two children at a time. The child pension is converted to orphan pension in the
event of demise of the surviving parent and the orphan pension is more than the child pension.

h) The insurance benefit (Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance, 1976) has also been enhanced from
maximum of Rs. 1,30,000/- to maximum of Rs. 3,60,000/- w.e.f. 1.9.2014.

Page 1 of 2

i) Online Transfer Claims Portal (OTCP) has been launched to facilitate transfer of member accounts,
once they change their job/location.

j} 99% payments to members made electronically via NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer).
The facility of Corporate Cheque Payable at Par (CCPAP) has been introduced to eliminate frauds
in payments being made to members through cheques. In this facility once a payment is issued
against a particular cheque number, the same is intimated to the State Bank of India, the bankers
to EPFO, Subsequently, whenever this cheque is presented for payment, the system will permit
encashment of the cheque only against the amount authorized by EPFO. This facility is functional
in all EPF offices across India.

k) 100% payments to pensioners are being made electronically through the use of CORE banking
platform of banks through which pensions are being paid.

1) All employees working in the Building & Construction industry and drawing wages up to Rs.
15,000/- per month are to be compulsorily enrolled as members under the Schemes (Employees'
Provident Funds Scheme 1952, Employees' Pension Scheme 1995 and Employees’ Deposit
Linked Insurance Scheme 1976) framed under the Act.

3. It is felt that the above steps taken by EPFO are not reaching the workers. It is thus decided that regular
awareness camps be organized particularly in industrial areas and residential areas where there is
concentration of unorganized labour for sensitizing them about their eligibility for availing social security benefits
provided by EPFO while implementing the Act and the Schemes framed thereunder.

4. Further, while organizing such awareness camps, the grievances of the workers pertaining to
settlement of amounts lying in inoperative accounts be redressed. Members who know the PF account number
be guided as to how they can get their money back lying in inoperative accounts. Similarly, members who do
not know the PF account number, at least the details of the establishments last served be collected and the PF
account numbers be ascertained from the office concemed and passed on to the members.

5. The feedback should be reported to Head Office on regular intervals.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Strategy to Reduce Inoperative Accounts by Identification and Refund of
balance to the beneficiaries.

Sir,

It was mentioned at the highest level on the occasion of Shramyev Jayate held on 16"
October 2014 that the amount of accumulation pertaining to beneficiaries which have become
inoperative shall be returned to the rightful persons. The task of EPFO is to secure the financial
benefits particularly in old age to persons joining the Scheme. In its fiduciary capacity it is
responsibility of EPFO to refund the money to the beneficiaries for and on behalf of whom the

money has been collected.

2, In absence of availability of address of the beneficiary, the task though may be onerous

has to be performed in time bound manner with active help and support of employers.

3. The inoperative accounts are presently being settled as on date as per the existing
process elaborated in circular No. WSU/Inoperative Accounts/6184 dated 28.07.2014. The
process in respect of application made by the account holder in its own volition shall remain

identical. For ready reference, copy of the circular is enclosed.

4. The issue of inoperative account has been discussed in a series of meeting held by CPFC.
Every RO has been instructed to organize camp to ensure that money goes to the rightful
claimant. Copy of the Email dated 18.08.2014 addressed to each RPFC/OIC is enclosed for ready

reference.

5. It has been observed that despite the express instructions, the progress in the area of
reduction in inoperative account is not adequate. A concerted effort in this matter is needed. The

following needs to be done immediately: -

e Identification of inoperative accounts.

e Reconciliation of same from the existing records to confirm the exact amount due
to the beneficiary.

e Ascertaining UAN of current employment of the beneficiary in case the
beneficiary is currently under employment and has a UAN.

e Transferring the amount from inoperative account to the current account by
linking the UAN.

e Ascertaining the present address of the beneficiary with help of employer in case
employee is not currently working.

e Getting the amount standing in the account refunded to the identified beneficiary.

6. It has been observed that there a large number of accounts which are presently
inoperative wherein the final settlement through withdrawal has already been affected. However,
subsequent to the withdrawal, an amount has been received in these accounts due to remittance
of dues by the employer; collection of additional amount consequent to assessment under 7A;
and collection of the dues so assessed. The amount might also come due to transfer of an
amount in the account from other offices. Amount might have also due to calculation and credit
of interest subsequent to withdrawal particularly if the settkement had taken place prior to 2007

as per the then Scheme provisions.

7. The Manual of Accounting Procedure at para No. 10.11.2 provides the following:-

“In case of defaulting establishments, the claim should be settled to the extent the amount
standing to the credit of the member, balance as and when realized from the defaultinz establishment,

should be released with interest as admissible under Para 60 of the EPF Scheme, 1952."

To this category of withdrawal process, all the cases where subsequent collection has
been made through the process of assessment under 7A and collection of additional amount so
assessed should also be included. Similarly, all the cases where withdrawal has already been
made but subsequent credit due to transfer in or calculation of interest has been affected should
also be included in this category. Interest to these additional amount of credit should be made
only as per the existing provisions in paragraph No. 72(6) read along with paragraph 60(6) of
the EPF Scheme, 1952.

8. The address and the bank account number of such inoperative account is likely to be
available in the system as these information are stored in the database at the time of settlement

of first claim of withdrawal.

9. The process of this settlement does not require any application to be made by the
beneficiary.

Subject : Issue of notices to defaulting establishments on initiation of proceedings under Section
7A/14B of the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 through
e-mail - regarding

Sir,

A facility for Online Registration of Establishments (OLRE) has been provided for the employers to get
themselves registered under the Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 (the Act) for
Provident Fund code number.

2. Establishments are now required to register themselves online for PF code number. While registering
themselves the employers are required to fill up Form 5A regarding particulars of all the branches and departments,
owners, occupiers, directors, partners, manager or any other person or persons who have the ultimate control over the
affairs of such factory or establishment in e-format. A provision has also been made in the Form 5A to register the email id of the establishment. It has also been instructed that the existing establishments are also required to fill up
Form SA online.

3. As per the existing practice, whenever proceedings are initiated either under Section 7A of the Act for
deciding applicability/assessment of dues against the defaulting establishments or under Section 14B of the Act for
levy of damages, notices are issued to the establishments by post.

4, Now, since the employers provide their e-mail id in Form 5A, it has been decided that in addition to notices
issued by post, notices shall also be sent in the e-mail id of the establishment.

5. This shall be strictly adhered to.
(This issues with the approval of CPFC.)

Yours faithfully,

Sir,

Vide this office letter no. BSC/12(202007-08/14432 dated 11.11.2013 all that
RPFCs / Officers and Staff who joined after 01.01.2004 were advised to apply for PRAN.
Further, vide this office circular no, BSC-12(2)2007-08/NPS/Staff/VolII/3748 dated
13.05.2014 communicating that the rate of interest to be given on the arrears of NPS
accumulations (Legacy Data) shall carry the same rate of interest as applicable on GPF from
01.01.2004 onwards. It was further clarified that the GPF rate of interest shall be given on
arrear payments only and in no case beyond 31.05.2014.

2. It was also communicated that it shall be the responsibility of DDOs to ensure that
payments are effected to NSDL in time and it shall not attract any interest at all for delayed
transfers.

be implemented from the date of decision of 190% CBT meeting held on 15.09.2010, were
placed before the 80% meeting of EC on 18.12.2014 and 205” meeting of CBT on
19.12.2014. It was decided that no prospective / retrospective implementation of NPS for
officers and staff is possible and it be in tune with Central Government Scheme w.e.f.
01.01.2004.

~ You are therefore advised to direct all the officers and staff to apply for PRAN by
6% January, 2015 failing which apart from denial of interest on arrears administrative action
will be taken. ?

5. A list of officers / staff who don’t have applied for PRAN till date be sent to us by
7% January, 2015.

Subject: EDL! Exemption Proposal - [nsisting for minimum premium of 0.5% of
wages in schemes offered in lieu of EDLI - clarification - regarding.

Sir,

It has come to the notice of Headquarters that many offices while examining or
processing EDLI exemption proposals are insisting upon the criteria of minimum
premium of 0.5% of the wages to be paid by the employer in the schemes offered by
Insurance Service Providers in lieu of EDLI. In some cases instructions or directives

have also been issued to the establishments / employers as well in this regard.

2. It is possible that this may have been done on the basis of the deliberations in the
Meeting of the Zonal Additional Central Commissioners held on 07 and 08t® March,
2014 at Headquarters where this issue was discussed. The matter has been examined
and itis seen that the provisions of exemption from EDLI Scheme both under the EPF &
MP Act, 1952 and the EDLI, 1976 Scheme do not sustain or support the criteria for
insisting that the premiums payable by the employer in EDLI exemption cases should

not be less than the statutory contributions of 0.5% of the wages.

7. Accordingly, field offices may not insist upon this criterion while processing
EDLI exemption matters and if any instructions or directives have been issued to

employers or establishments from the field offices in this regard, the same may be

recalled.
Yours faithfully,

Subject:

CPFC from
being

a
respondent
in routine
manner in appeals and contempt cases pertaining to 7A/14B,
14 etc.- Regarding.
Sir,
It
has been experienced
that
Central
P.F. Commissioner
is invariably
impleaded as respondent in cases at different legal fora.
1. You are
requested
to
take
necessary
action
for
avoiding
Central
P.F.
Commissioner
from
being
made a respondent
in a routine
manner
in
appeals/contempt
cases pertaining to 7A/14B, 14 etc.
2. Often, there
is little
merit
in making CPFC a party
in either
of the two
categories of cases. Such inclusion of CPFC results in huge waste of time
and resources of the Organisation.
Beside, the matter sometimes escalates
to such a point that Courts pass Contempt Notice against CPFC. This can
be avoided to a certain extent by taking appropriate
legal steps.
3. With regard to the first category of case, the CPFCis neither an Appellate
Authority
nor is responsible for 7A /14B/Recovery
Orders passed by the
competent
Officers of the Regions. These are judicial
orders and can only
be appealed against in the higher court such as the EPFAppellate Tribunal
or a High Court. Hence, the inclusion of CPFCas one of Respondents is a
Misjoinder of party under Order 1 of the Civil Procedure Code, 1908.
4. Similarly,
if the CPFCis made one of the Respondents on behalf of the CBT
( EPF) in the second category
of cases, then it can be pleaded by the
concerned
RO/SRO that the APFC/EO ( legal) of the concerned RO/SRO
signing the Written
Statement
on behalf of the Organisation
or the CBT
(EPF), is a competent authority to do so under Section-SE of the EPF& MP
Act and therefore there is no need to make CPFCOR ANY OTHEROfficer as
a Respondent in the case.

5. All the
ROs/SROs of EPFO requested to file
necessary applications
in
concerned Court for deletion of CPFC as a party,
in the first
instance
alongwith their Written Statement, the instructions must be followed in its
letterand
sprit.
Yours faithfully,

Sub:-Release of functionalities
on UAN portal for displaying the
Universal Account Number (UAN) by member directly and for
making request by an old member for allotment of UAN.
Sir,
During various review meetings
of UAN programme,
it was noted that
some employers
have not disseminated
UAN to the EPF members. Though a
facility already exists on UAN portal whereby a member can check the fact of
allotment
of
UAN
to
him/her
based
upon
his
member
ID,
the
nondissemination
of UAN by employer
have resulted
in a number of grievances
by members.
The matter
was deliberated
upon and it was decided that the
above facility should be extended to display of the Universal Account Number
to such queries.
2.
Accordingly a functionality
has been developed to provide the facility to
display
the
Universal
Account
Number
through
UAN portal
directly.
The
facility
requires the member to furnish
his P.F. member ID, name (as per PF
records)
and date of birth
for validation
against
data in EPF masters.
The
member is required to furnish his mobile number, where One Time Pin (OTP)
would
be sent leading to authentication
of the mobile
number.
It is to be
noted that
same mobile
number
cannot
be used more than
once for this
purpose.
The
detailed
process
flow
for
the
functionality
is
placed
at

Annexure-A.
The same is also being placed on UAN member
e-sewa
portal
for the convenience
of members.
3.
Also during
discussions at various
forms,
it has been noted that there
is a demand for allotment
of UAN to old members
(who are presently
not in
employment).
The matter
was discussed
and it was decided
that
the
UAN
would be allotted
to such members on request basis. A functionality
has been
provided
on UAN portal for the purpose whereby
the member
can submit
his
request through
UAN Member e-sewa portal.
A detailed
process flow for the
functionality
is placed at Annexure-B.
4.
All the field offices
are requested
to take
note of the above facilities
available
on the portal for the convenience
of the members.
The field offices
are
advised
to
carry
out
awareness
campaign
to
spread
the
awareness
amongst
members to facilitate
them to benefit from UAN programmes.
5.
Any suggestions
and feedbacks on the above facilities
are welcome and
may be forwarded
to Information
Services Division immediately.
Yours faithfully,

Sub:- Order of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, New Dethi [R.K.
Verma Vs. APFC, Karnal & others (Appeal No. 494/2013)].
Sir,
In continuation to this office circular letter of even number dated 14-11-2013 in which
_ State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Haryana, Panchkula order dated 02-09-2013
was circulated.

2. State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission. Haryana, Panchkula in its order had
held that there is no provision in the EPS, 1995 for restoration of commuted pension, and
therefore once a pensioner opted for commutation, such pensioner is entitled only for balance
pension on monthly basis.

3. The petitioner filed a Revision Petition No. 4545/2013 against the order dated 02-09-2013
of State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Haryana, Panchkula in the National
Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, New Delhi. The National Consumer Disputes
Redressal Commission, New Delhi has also been accepted the above contention in its order
dated 18-11-2014. A copy of the said order is enclosed.

4. in the order of National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, it has been held that —

“A member of Employees Pension Scheme on his retirement has an option whether
to avail off the full pension or to commute a part of the pension and receive the lumpsum
amount in lieu thereof. Clause 13(2) of Employees Pension Scheme, 1995 stipulates that
the option if exercised is final and not revocable. The scheme does not provide for
restoration of commuted pension after expiry of stipulated period. In the instant case,
admittedly the petitioner opted for commutation of his pension under the scheme and
received the lumpsum amount in lieu of the commuted portion of pension. Thus, in view of
Rule 13(2) of the scheme, the petitioner after having exercised his option cannot claim the
restoration of the commuted portion of pension. The respondent department while
denying to restore the commuted pension has acted in accordance with Rule 13 of
Employees Pension Scheme, 1995. Therefore, it cannot be said to be deficient in service.”

Accordingly, in similar legai disputes, the judgment may also be cited and utilised.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Dashboard for monitoring
UAN activities-Regarding.
Sir,
The UAN Programme, currently under implementation
in the Organisation,
has two distinct stages - firstly the allotment
of UAN to all the members where
the contributions
have been received during the period from
1st January, 2014
and 30th June, 2014 and secondly the incremental
activities.
The second stage
involves the allotment
of UAN to the new members joining the fund for the first
time and tagging the present employment
to existing
UAN of the members on
their shifting of the jobs. The seeding and verification
of KYC details is of critical
importance in both the stages.
2.
Earlier
two
dashboards
i.e
UAN -
KYC Dashboard
and
UAN -
KYC
Missing
Bank
Details
Dashboard
have
been
provided
for
monitoring
the activities
relating to KYC seeding in UAN database. To monitor
the UAN activities for incremental
membership i.e. those where the contributions
have
been
received
after
30th
June,
2014,
a
dashboard
under
the
name
Dashboard
for
Monitoring
the
UAN
activities
for
Incremental
Membership
has been provided
on EPFO website
under the link "For EPF
office use". The username and password has already been sent to the official email 1D of all the offices.
3.
The
description
of
each
of
the
columns
has
been
explained
in the
Annexure for understanding
various columns and monitoring
the activities. The
field offices are required to monitor the pendency at columns at (C), (D) and (J)
for the smooth and effective functioning of UAN programme.

4.
It is to be noted that the pendency as indicated in Column (C) relates to
field
office due to
non-availability
of these
member
accounts
in the
Member
Master in OTCP.The possible reasons for the same could be as follows:
(a)
The
ECR of the
relevant
month
has not
been
uploaded
in the
application software after downloading it from ECR portal.
(b)
The ECRof the relevant month has been uploaded in the application
software but has not been reconciled with the bank statement.
(c)
The ECRof the relevant month has been uploaded and reconciled in
the
application
software,
but the
accounting
year
has not been
released for the first time in respect of the establishment.
(d)
All the activities as in (a), (b) and (c) above have been carried out,
but the Member Master has not been updated on OTCP.
5.
The pendency as detailed in Column (D) relates to the employer.
It is to
be noted that
that
for new members joining
an establishment,
there
are two
possibilities:
(i) The new member doesn't have any previous P.F. membership.
Such member
is to be identified
by the employer
for allotment
of Universal Account Number
(UAN) by EPFO.
(ii) The new member has a previous P.F. membership which is to be linked with
the present
member
10 through
his Universal Account
Number
(UAN). There
would be auto generation
of transfer request in case the KYC details seeded with
UAN are
also
approved
by
present
employer
using
his
Digital
Signature
Certificate registered with EPFO.
6.
It is to be noted that transfer
request is auto-generated
only if the UAN
database
of the
member
is seeded with the defined
KYC details
by previous
employer
and the same KYC details are verified
by the present employer. The
defined
KYCs details for the purpose are Bank Account
Number and either of
Aadhar or PAN.
7.
Though
the
transfer
request
is
auto-generated,
if
the
above
mentioned
criteria
of KYC is met, the services including
portability
are
available to the members
only after activation
of UAN member
e-sewa
portal on EPFO website. The Column (J) provides details of all such cases
where the transfer
request has been auto-generated
but it is pending at

portal
due to

Subject: Creation of Staff Grievance Handling System (SGHS) — Regarding

Sir/Madam,

Various staff members had raised their individual HR-related grievances to
CPFC, while he was on tour to the field offices. The field units of the EPF Staff
Federations had also intimated many such grievances. Similarly, grievances
/representations are regularly being received in the CPFC secretariat at Head Office
from all over India. Some of the grievances are related to issues pending at SubRegional /Regional Offices and some of the grievances are related to policies which are
being framed at Head Office level. At present, in the manual system of Dak
management, there is a possibility of losing out many of those individual grievances
raised by employees to the voluminous amount of dak/papers etc.

2. The CPFC in the meetings with the EPF Staff Federation as well as EPF
Officers’ Association had announced for creation of an online system of handling staff
grievances for systematic redressal of grievances of our own employees/
officers/Pensioners and family pensioners. As per the direction of the CPFC, HRM
Division, in consultation with IS division, is considering to establish an on line system of
filing of such grievances by the individual employees/officers.

3. The salient features of the SGHS at its initial stage will be as follows:

a. All the employees/ officers/ pensioners/family pensioners are eligible to submit
their grievances / representations through this facility at their individual level.
Any anonymous/pseudonymous and representations raised by any person other
than those, who are made eligible to raise their individual grievance will be
rejected ab initio without assigning any reasons.

b. This facility of filing representations/grievances is not available to the
recongnised/unrecognized staff federations or group of employees and officers
under any name or banner.

c. Under this scheme, eligible individual can register their grievances through an
online fillable form, which shall be available on the EPF Website from
08.12.2014(FN)to 31.12.2014 (AN).

d. The eligible individual is again required to register his/her grievances through
this system, even if he/she had filed any representation through manual mode
before.

e. The eligible individual should not file any following type of grievances:

i. Grievances raised in the past that stand disposed.
ii. Grievances for which the individual has filed any application before the
judiciary.

4. In view of above, it is requested that the Scheme may be brought to the notice of
all eligible individuals for necessary actions, if any .

(This issues with the approval of the CPFC)

Sir,

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a five days

to 12" Dec 2014 in its premises at -

e Explain the various compliance provisions of the EPF and MP Act, 1952

e Inspect the Books / Records of Exempted Establishments

e Explain the various Provisions available for Recovery of dues under the EPF and MP Act, 1952 and

e Explain the provisions of International Workers.

e Apply the learning for developing an integrated approach.

You are requested to nominate one officer from your Regional/Sub Regional Office who is holding the

ensured that no officer who is retiring in this financial may be nominated.

Sub:- Grant of financial upgradation under MACP Scheme in respect of eligible
officials in the cadre of Social Security Assistant — regarding

Sir,

This office has received various references from field offices for grant of financial
upgradation in the SSA cadre under MACP Scheme. As per provisions of MACP Scheme,
officials are being given the next grade pay after 10/20/30 year service, subject to certain
conditions. Earlier in ACP Scheme, prior to 01/09/2008, the officials were getting the
financial] benefit of the next promotional pay after 12/24 years of service.

The cadre of Social Security Assistant in the pay scale of Rs. 4000-6000 (pre-revised)
corresponding to the pay band of Rs. 5200-20200 with grade pay of Rs. 2400 was introduced
in EPFO. The Recruitment Rules to the said post was notified on 03/01/2014. Vide Head
office letter dated 15/11/2007, the financial upgradation in the cadre of Social Security
Assistant was provided in the pay scale of Rs. 4500-7000 (pre-revised) corresponding pay
band of Rs. 5200-20200 with grade pay of Rs. 2800 on completion of 04 years regular
service. Subsequently, the upgradation in the pay scale of Rs. 5000-8000 (pre-revised)
corresponding the pay band of Rs. 9300-34800 with grade pay of Rs. 4200 was provided
against the 60% of total sanctioned strength of SSA.

Some of the offices have conducted the Screening Committee meeting in connection
with extending the benefit of financial upgradation in eligible persons in SSA cadre under
MACP Scheme to SSSA and sent the proceeding/recommendations of the Screening
Committee meeting in Head office seeking approval. It is observed that after going through
the ACR/APAR dossiers for the last 5 years and other relevant service records, including
vigilance clearance certificate issued by Zonal Vigilance Directorate, the committee has
recommended the eligible official in the cadre of SSSA for extension of benefit of financial
upgradation under MACP Scheme in the grade pay of Rs. 4600.

Para 13 to Annexure of the MACP Scheme states that Existing Time Bound
-Promotion Scheme, including in-situ promotion scheme, or any other kind of promotion
scheme shall not run concurrently with the MACPs. Hence, the matter has been referred to
Government seeking clarification as to whether grant of financial upgradation under
MACP Scheme in respect of eligible candidates can be provided together the financial
upgradation granted to SSAs to the grade pay of Rs. 2800 and Rs. 4200. It is, therefore,
requested to look into the matter and furnish the details of such cases where benefit of
financial upgradation under MACP Scheme in the grade pay of Rs. 4600/- has been
provided to the Social Security Assistant by the RPFC/ACC(Zone). Further action in the
cases of financial upgradation under MACP Scheme in the cadre of Social Security
Assistant will be taken after getting the clarification of the Government.

Yours faithfully,

The Central Board of trustees in its 157 meeting had approved the proposal for

offer the Group Term Product conferring similar or better benefits than the Employees’ Deposit
Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976 for the purpose for grant of exemption from the Employee's
Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.

Organization for approval of the IndiaFirst Group Term Plan offered by them for issuance in lieu
of Employee’s Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976{copy of Master Policy enclosed). The
salient features of this policy are as under:-

i) The policy is arranged to provide Assurance benefits to the employees with the
condition that the benefits under the said policy shall not be less than the
benefits provided under the Employee’s Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme, 1976.

ii) All members of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 in the company
will be eligible to be members of the policy. The member becomes eligible for
the coverage as soon as he/she becomes the member of the Employees’
Provident Funds Scheme, 1952.

iii) No member shall withdraw from the scheme as long as he satisfies the
conditions of eligibility described above.

iv) The employer (policy holder) will give an undertaking to the effect that all new
members have been Included from the date of their joining. If a death claim is

The National Academy for Training and Research in Social Security (NATRSS) is conducting a three
days programme on “Financial Management in EPFO” scheduled to be held from 19 November to 215
November 2014 in its premises at -

30-31 Institutional Area, D-Block, Janak Puri, New Delhi-110058.
The course shall have the following learning objectives:

e Understand accounting principles and practices followed in govt. in general and Employees’
Provident Fund Organisation in particular.

e Describe basic concepts of preparing Balance Sheet and Budget in Employees’ Provident Fund

Organisation.

Describe Banking and Investment of Funds.

Explain subscriber and Establishment accounting.

Describe New Fund Management System.

Maintain and reconcile Cash Book.

You are requested to nominate one officer from your region who is holding the charge of APFC
(Accounts), APFC (Cash) or RPFC (F&A).

The name of the nominated officer may please be communicated latest by 12* November 2014.

programme till one day after the completion of the training programme. Any extension beyond this will
require specific approval of Director, NATRSS.

You are requested to relieve the officer(s) with a direction to report to NATRSS on 19 November

Sub: Pending Public Grievances - Reg.
Sir

As you are aware that as on date all public grievances are to be necessarily registered and disposed of
through EPFIGMS, so as to ensure that grievances are properly recorded, redressed, managed and analysed.

However, on analyzing the pendency report of grievances generated through EPFIGMS, it appears that
the registration of grievances in EPFIGMS may not be regular at many offices which are showing negligible & in
some case almost nil receipt of public grievances.

Accordingly, it Is requested that the Officer-In-Charge may personally review the registration of
grievances received at least once in a week to ensure that all grievances whether received through e-mail,
post or any other mode are invariably registered at the earliest under EPFIGMS. Further the Officer-in-Charge
may also review the disposal of the grievances and establish the practice to seek feedback in respect of at
least few disposed cases so as to ensure that the disposals are correct and proper.

In this regard, a list of 43 ROs/SROs is also enclosed herewith which have more than 10 cases pending
as on date as per EPFIGMS for information and tmmediate action specially where the grievance is pending for
more than 30 days. The remaining offices are also advised to immediately refer EPFIGMS to ensure
registration and disposal of all Public Grievances,

It Is also noticed that in respect of some ROs/SROs while the individual RO/SROs are reflecting
comparatively lower level of pending grievances whereas number of grievances pertaining to the same offices
forwarded by Head Office and accordingly, being refiected pending against the concerned CSD Section at Head
Office Is comparatively much higher.

This is surprising and only one of two inferences can be drawn by this anomaly j.e. either such
ROs/SROs are giving least priority to cases forwarded by Head Office or the grievances handling at their end is
prompting more & more members/beneficiaries to lodge grievances with Head Office instead of the concerned
office,

Accordingly, Officer-in-Charges are once again requested to take personal interest in the work related

to redressal of public grievances so as to constructively help in image building of the organization which can be
improved a lot by ensuring timely and proper redressal of public grievances.

Sub: Banking Agreement for Payment to the Overseas Bank Accounts of International
Workers and their beneficiaries— reg.

Sir,

Your kind attention is invited to the provisions relating to settlement of claims and
disbursement of benefits to overseas bank accounts of International Workers including their
beneficiaries. For ready reference the provisions relating to payment of Provident Fund in respect of
International Workers are reproduced as under:

“72. Payment of Provident Fund. — (1) When the amount standing to the credit of a member
becomes payable, it shall be the duty of the Commissioner to make prompt payment as provided in the
Scheme.

(2) The due amount in respect of the member shall be payable in the payees bank account
directly or through the employer.

(3) In all the other cases, the amount due shall be payable to the credit of payee's bank
account in India.

In view of the aforesaid provisions, the International Workers and their beneficiaries from the

SSA countries shall be seeking payment of benefits to their overseas bank account. In order to

facilitate such payments, Finance Division, after consultation with various stakeholders including SBI,

issued directions vide its letter No. Bkg./1(12)10/1WU/4211 dated 21.05.2014 to RPFC, Delhi (North)

Minutes of the decisions taken in the meeting the Addl. CPFC (HQrs) had with the
representatives of the Federation of All India Pensioners Associations of the EPF
Organisation on 10.09.2014 at 11.00 A.M in his office chamber.

7K KOK

The statement of action taken on the various issues raised by the Federation was
taken up for discussion.

Issue No.1- Framing of a Scheme/Rules for providing medical facilities to the pensioners
and their dependents.

(a) | The Federation Welcomed the formation of a committee of officers and refrence
made to Director,NATRSS to examine the Draft Medical Attendance Rules submitted by the
Secretary General of the Federation Shri B.Raja and to formulate a scheme to provide
cashless medicare facilities to the pensioners and their dependents. Shri B.Raja was advised
to attend the meeting to be taken by the Director NATRSS on 11.09.2014 at 11.00 A.M. The
facts that the RPFCs of Hyderabad, and Koltata have entered into M.O.Us with six hospitals
each and that the clarification sought by the Zonal Office of TN & KR has been referred to
the HR committee have been noted. The ACCs (MH & Goa) and Gujarat & M.P. have ‘demi’
officially been reminded of the subjects was also taken note of.

(b) | The Federation brought to the notice the Add. CPFC that there was no response from
any hospital in Bangalore to the letter of intent called for by the RPFC.

(c) The Federation side insisted that in all cases where the patients claim reimbursement
of expenses incurred by them for taking treatment in any hospital recognized by the
State/Central Govt. should be fully paid in the light of the series of CAT orders which have
been confirmed by the High Court/s. The Federation also brought to the notice of the Addl.
CPFC HQrs. the fact that three more pensioners in Bangalore have moved the Karnataka
Bench of the CAT seeking for appropriate directions to the RPFC as their claims were not

settled fully despite the detailed clarificatory letter issued by the Central Office on
16.06.2014.

(d) Federation also complained about delay in settlement of medical bills of Pensioners —
due to negative attitude of RPFCs of Bangalore & Odisha.The position that no medical bill of
pensioners was pending in the R.O. Bangalore and that the RPFC Odisha’s report when the
Addl. CPFC spoke to him in the midst of the discussion that only two bills pending in the R
Bhubaneswar are under process was noted with satisfaction by the Federation.ACC also
spoke to ACC(Karnataka & Goa) to call meeting of RPFC in Karnataka regarding
empanelment of hospitals for extending cashless medical facility to pensioners.

12:

2. Issue of photo I.D. cards with more details.

The Federation desired that the pensioners should be issued Photo I.D. cards as was
agreed upon in the meeting the Delhi Association had with the Addl. CPFC in Nov.2013 with
details of the age/date of birth of the spouse and the pay last drawn at the time of
retirement (which will determine the entitlement of the patient for hospital accommodation).
The Federation also handed over a Xerox copy of the I.D. card issued by R.O. West Bengal.
The Federation also suggested that the new I.D. card to be issued be made valid for the life
of the pensioner and its validity should not be limited to 5 years as has been specified in the
I.D. cards already issued.

It was agreed that the Central Office will devise a Plastic card and advice all the

RPFCs etc to issue fresh Plastic I.D. cards. If any one looses the card he should bear the
cost of new card.

3. Long pendency of vigilance cases and consequential sufferings of pensioners facing
disciplinary cases.

The Federation emphasized the urgent need for speedy disposal of all disciplinary
cases within a reasonable time say one year or so from the date of initiation of the
proceedings as otherwise the pensioners are facing a stigma in the Society and even the
family members do not respect the pensioner. Atleast in cases not requiring major penalties
gratuity should be paid as according to the Supreme Court gratuity and pension are
properties of an employee earned after long services in the Govt. which cannot be denied
even in cases where criminal cases are pending.

The Federation was advised to take up the issue with the Director of Vigilance for an
appropriate solution.

4. Revision of pay scales of E.Os/AAOs and other staff in the ROs.

The Federation pleaded that the amendment to the recruitment rules of Section
Officers in the HQrs office has in no way disturbed the existing arrangement of treating the
cadres of EOs/AAOs and Section Officers as feeder cadres for promotion to the APFC cadre,

and therefore there was a justification to prepone the date of pay revision of EOs/AOs etc to
01.04.2004 as in the case of section officers.

The Addl. CPFC informed that the matter has been referred to HRD section and that
section is being reminded to take necessary action.

5. Unauthorised recovery of interest from Pensioners in Gujarat Region on over
payments made.

The association was asked to provide list of specific cases in this regard as RPFCs of
Gujrat region have denied of making any such recovery.

6. Transfer of service records of pensioners of Nagpur & Pune Regions from R.O.
Bandra.

Sir,

Please refer to this Office letter No. HRM-!I/A.10(3)2007/DR APFC/Pt.1/16232 dated

PF Commissioners to call them and engage them in training work. The training is a very
important area in laying the strong and basic foundation of knowledge and. skill
development for the new APFCs and also to catch the higher level of foundation/ induction
training programme at NATRSS. Hence, seriousness needs to be given ‘On the Job’ Training.
If any new Direct Recruit does not concentrate/put efforts for ‘On the Job’ training then it
should be specifically reported to Head Office so that a decision to extend his probation
period could be taken or other disciplinary action could be taken. All concerned new DR
APFCs_ should be made clear that their confirmation also depends upon satisfactory
completion of training work (‘On the Job’ training as well as Induction Course training at
NATRSS).

in respect of each of the new Direct Recruits alongwith your remarks. On completion of the
‘On the Job’ training, the concerned RPFCs/OICs/ACCs should certify that the training
module already intimated has been followed and gone through by the concerned APFCs
direct recruits.

4. The training for next batch (3 batch) will start from 27™ October at NATRSS. If any
one of the Direct Recruit APFC has not undergone ‘On the Job’ training he need not be sent
for training and rather he be asked to complete ‘On the Job’ training and other action
should also be proposed by RPFC like extension of probation, stoppage of pay, disciplinary
action for their failure to undertake ‘On the Job’ training.
