Sub:- Submission of Proposal for Revised Estimate for the year 2014-2015 and
Budget Estimates for the year 2015-2016 for Capital Expenditure.

Sir,

This refers to Office Memorandum No: Budget/44/2014-15/2015-16/Main dated
03-09-2010, whereby the Chief Engineer (H.O.) has been requested to.-

“furnish the figures in respect of Original Works under ‘Capital Expenditure’,
office wise with detailed justification by 15°” October 2014. The proposal relating to
Capital Expenditure in r/o Andhra Pradesh should be strictly bifurcated into
Telangana and Andhra Pradesh Region”.

As you may be aware that para 9.3.1 of the MAP Part | provides that:-

“As far as the expenditure towards the Capital nature is concerned the Chief
Engineer the Organisation will examine the proposals on Capital Expenditure and
petty works, & maintenance and finalise the same for consolidating the budget
proposals”

Accordingly, it is requested that by 9 October, 2014 the necessary budget
proposals for all original work of capital expenditure may be forwarded by the RPFC | of
the Region in respect of Region as a whole i.e keeping in view the requirement of SROs
also by consolidating the proposals of Regional Office and Sub-Regional-Office in
connection of all original work of Capital Expenditure to this office in the Performa
attached as Annexure A.

While forwarding budget proposals it may be kept in mind that RPFC shall be
responsible for ‘utilization of the budget sanctioned. Accordingly Budget estimates be
' prepared carefully by keeping in view the requirement as well as the usual time taken in

obtaining administrative approval/sanction as well as the periodicity of releasing the
sanctioned amount.

For example in respect of all the offices where new construction projects are likely
to start by end of December 2014, adequate budget provision in RE 2014-15 shall be
made for the first payment to be released to the PWO. Whereas, for remaining payments
depending upon the Estimates submitted and timelines agreed to suitable provision may
be made in RE 2014-15 ; BE 2015-16 or thereafter in subsequent budget exercises.

Please note that all administrative sanctions and approvals are made subject to
availability of Budget. Therefore, necessary Budget provisions must be made by the
concerned RPFC to avoid seeking budget from the Central pool which can be released
only by CPFC in only such cases where expenditure cannot be foreseen.

Further, please also note that budget is a tool of Financial Planning and therefore
allotment of budget does not mean administrative approval/sanction and the same must
be obtained from the competent authority for utilizing the allocated budget.

(This issues with the approval of ACC (HR)/ In-charge Chief Engineer)

Sub: Declaration of Productivity Linked Bonus (P.L.B.) for the employees of the
EPFO for the year 2013-2014.

Sir,

The Central Government, in terms of Section 5D(7) of the Employees’ Provident Funds
& Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952, has conveyed its approval to the extension of the
existing Productivity Linked Bonus Scheme for the year 2013-2014 vide their letter No A26022/1/1994-SS.1 dated 1 October 2014.

2, Accordingly, the Competent Authority is pleased to convey the approval for payment of
the Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 2013-2014 for 60 (Sixty) days in all the
offices of EPFO. The bonus of 60 days has been assessed on the basis of Performance
Report forwarded by the Regional Offices in compliance to Head Office letter dated
10.09.2014. The payment of bonus is to be released to all Group ‘C’ and Group ‘B’ (NonGazetted) employees of EPFO.

3. The terms and conditions governing payment of P.L.B. will be as per the instructions
issued by the Government of India for payment of the bonus to the employees in Central
Government departments from time to time. However, the quantum of bonus may be
assessed as per the following formula circulated vide Govt. of India, Ministry of Finance O.M.
No. 14(1) E.Co-ord.1/2004 dated 30.9.2004.

= (AVERAGE EMOLUMENTS) X (NUMBER OF DAYS OF BONUS)
30.4*

(* Average number of days in a month)

4. The maximum amount of bonus will be restricted to the amount admissible to those
drawing emoluments of Rs.3,500/- per month. The bonus in respect of the employees drawing
emoluments of more than Rs.3,500/- per month will be calculated as if the emoluments were
Rs.3,500/- per month.

-25. The term ‘emoluments’ occurring in these orders will include Basic Pay, Personal Pay,
Special Pay, Deputation (Duty) Allowance and Dearness Allowance, but will not include other
Allowances, such as HRA, CCA Special Compensatory (Remote locality) Allowance, Bad Climate
Allowance, Children Education Allowance and Interim Relief etc.

6. The expenditure incurred for payment of bonus may be debited from the budget head
“Productivity Linked Bonus.”

Yours faithfully,

(Sanjay Kuprar)
FA&CAO

आजिहादद हद नहदगां थध, बजलक एक सस्वचच एस्वगां वस्वकससत दनश कक कलपनहा भध थध।
महहातमहा गहागांधध नन गगलहामध कक जिगांजिधरर कक तकड़कर महाम भहारतध कक आजहाद करहायहा।
अब हमहारहा कतरवय हनै कक गगांदगध कक ददर करकन भहारत महातहा कक सनस्वहा करम।
मम शपथ लनतहा हदगां कक मम सस्वयगां सस्वचचतहा कन प्रतत सजिग रहदगांगहा और उसकन सलए
समय ददगांगहा।
हर स्वरर 100 घगांटन यहानध हर सपतहाह 2 घगांटन श्रमदहान करकन सस्वचचतहा कन इस
सगांकलप कक चररतहाथर करगांगहा।
मम न गगांदगध करगांगहा न ककसध और कक करनन ददगांगहा।
सबसन पहलन मम सस्वयगां सन, मनरन पररस्वहार सन, मनरन मगहललन सन, मनरन गहागांस्व सन एस्वगां मनरन
कहायरसथल सन शगरुआत करगांगहा।
मम यह महानतहा हदगां कक दगतनयहा कन जिक भध दनश सस्वचच ददखतन हम उसकहा कहारण
यह हनै कक स्वहहागां कन नहागररक गगांदगध नहदगां करतन और न हद हकनन दनतन हम।
इस वस्वचहार कन सहाथ मम गहागांस्व-गहागांस्व और गलद-गलद सस्वचच भहारत समशन कहा
प्रचहार करगांगहा।
मम आजि जिक शपथ लन रहहा हदगां, स्वह अनय 100 वयजकतयर सन भध करस्वहाऊगांगहा।
स्वन भध मनरद तरह सस्वचचतहा कन सलए 100 घगांटन दम, इसकन सलए प्रयहास करगांगहा।
मगझन महालदम हनै कक सस्वचचतहा कक तरर बढहायहा गयहा मनरहा एक कदम पदरन भहारत
दनश कक सस्वचच बनहानन मम मदद करनगहा।

To On 2 3 SEP 2014

All Officers and Staff Members of the EPFO,

As you are all aware that sudden flood have hit Jammu & Kashmir on 07-09-2014. It has taken heavy
toll of human life. The normal lives of lakhs of persons have been badly affected keeping them in utter
destitution, shambles and despair. The floods have also destroyed hundreds of crores of rupees worth
standing crops, cattle, roads, shops and other movable and immovable property. The victims of this tragedy,
therefore, need immediate assistance.

To render the help to the destitute, an extra ordinary meeting of the Central Staff Welfare
Committee was held on 22.09.2014 under the Chairmanship of Central Provident Fund Commissioner in
consonance with the Hon’ble Prime Minister appeal for sending contributions to the Prime Minister’s
National Relief Fund. The whole nation is concerned about helping the people of Jammu & Kashmir.

I know that the Employees of Employees’ Provident Fund Organization has a great history in helping
the nation on such disastrous occasions like Operation Vijay, Orissa Cyclone, Tsunami & Uttrakhand. The
Officers and staff of the EPF Organisation are showing their zeal and courage with tremendous commitment
by donating some money. Further those employees who are not willing to contribute may give in writing for
non deductions.

I, therefore, appeal to all Officers and staff of the Employees’ Provident Fund Organization to show
their sympathy and concern to the victims of Jammu & Kashmir flood tragedy and contribute on voluntary
basis, to say Rs. 200 from Group ‘C’ (MTS) and Rs. 300/- from other Group ‘C’, Rs. 500/- from Group ‘B’ ,Rs.
1000/- from Group ‘A’ and Rs. 2,000/- R.P.F.C. I and above to the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund. The
contributions to the Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund are exempted from Income Tax under Section 80G
of Income Tax Act.

As a token of immediate relief, a cheque of Rs. 51,00,000/- (Rupees Fifty one lakhs only) is being
issued in favour of Prime Minister ‘s Relief Fund from the Central Staff Welfare Committee. Deductions
made may kindly be deposited directly to EPF Central Staff Welfare Committee Account No.
31277572518 under intimation to the undersigned.

With best wishes

Yours faithfully,

Subject: Giving Publicity and Organizing felicitation Programmes for EPS95 Pensioners in all field offices

Sir,

As you are aware, the proposal for ensuring a minimum pension of Rs.
1,000/- per month for the member, family and disabled pensioners of the
Employees Pension Scheme, 1995 along with consequent increases in the children
and orphan pension amounts has been accepted and notified by the Government
vide Gazette Notification No. GSR-593(E) dated 19-Aug-14.

2. Out of the present 49-lakh odd pensioners of EPS-95 approximately 32 lakh
pensioners are drawing pensions of less than Rs. 1,000/- per month with a large
number of them drawing less than even Rs. 500/- per month as pension. The
initiative of ensuring a minimum pension of Rs. 1,000/- per month fulfills a longstanding aspiration of this category of EPS-95 pensioners for a reasonably decent
amount as monthly pension.

3. It has been felt that this initiative should be given appropriate adequate
publicity among the EPS pensioners as well as among the members / subscribers of
EPF. Towards this end all offices should undertake the following measures in their
respective offices:

a) In the first week of October 2014 all offices must issue a press release for all
the local newspapers and other publications stating that the proposal for
minimum pension of Rs. 1,000/- per month under the EPS-95 has been
implemented and that the pensioners would get the enhanced pension for
the month of September 2014 onwards. The press release should, inter-alia,
indicate the office specific statistics of the total number of pensioners and

the number of pensioners who were drawing pension less than Rs. 1,000/-
per month who would be the immediate and direct beneficiaries. Providing
this information slab-wise may also be considered. In this connection a few
drafts are being sent from Publicity Wing of headquarters.

b) All offices may organize a felicitation programme on 30-Sep-14 for EPS-95
pensioners where apart from formally announcing the implementation of
the enhanced minimum pension under the recent notification, pensioners
may be invited and felicitated. It may be explored whether it is possible to
have the pensioner of the oldest PPO issued by the office as well as the
pensioner drawing the least pension invited in the programme. Each office
may decide on the list of persons as well as the pensioners to be invited to
the programme. The concerned persons / authorities of pension disbursing
banks may also be invited.

c) The officers may also participate in local Radio and Television programmes
on social security in the period and give publicity in this regard.

d) In the felicitation programme mentioned above a separate slot may be kept
for redressing grievances of any pensioner or pension claim applicant. It
would be impactful and appropriate if the grievances can be taken up and
sorted out during the event itself.

4, At a few offices, the Government may designate dignitaries who will preside
over the felicitation functions. At such places the functions $hould be organized ina
commensurate manner. At other locations about 100-150 pensioners may be
invited and felicitated.

5. The expenditure on account of the above may be booked under the budget
head ‘Publicity’ and if additional fund sanction is required under the head, the
matter may be taken up with Finance Wing of headquarters through Regional
Offices. A report of the actions taken may be submitted to headquarters for
information.

[This issues with the approval of Central Provident Fund Commissioner]

Yours faithfully,

Subject: “BANK ACCOUNT RECONCILATION APPLICATION”- Web
Based Reconciliation Program.

Ref. Circular No. Bkg. 1(2)/2006/NFMS/Vol.V/22687 dated 29.01.2014 (Posted
at Sl. No. 699 on website)

Sir,

A program was launched vide above referred circular for web based
reconciltation of transfers between field offices’ accounts and central accounts wherein
all ROs/SROs were requested to upload the bank statement of all accounts (A/c No. 1, 2,
5, 11, 21 & 22) at the link http:/banking.epfoservices.org/Banking/ in addition to
sending date-wise transfer details of all accounts manually as well as through email till
further order.

3. Since web based reconciliation program is now running successfully, it has
been decided to discontinue monthly report on date-wise transfer details of all accounts
manually(by post) or through email.

4, Therefore, al! RO/SRO are requested not to send date-wise transfer details
of all accounts manually or through email. The practice of uploading bank statement of
all accounts (A/c No. 1, 2, 10, 1), 21 & 22) at fortnightly basis for reconciliation of
transfers between field accounts and central accounts shall continue. The bank statement
for the first fortnight be uploaded by 17" and for second fortnight by 2™ of the
succeeding month, incase of any holiday by the next date.

5. As per para 5.19.2(3) of the Agreement between EPFO & SBI, the day-end
balance (debit or credit) in the accounts of field offices, should be transferred online by
all the Link branches to the Central Investment Accounts. RPFC-II(F&A) at ROs and

APFC(Cash) at SROs may ensure that this para is implemented in true spirit by the
respective link branch.

Yours faithfully

Subject: Implementation of enhanced minimum pension - Bank
Reconciliation Statement (BRS) generation for the month of
September, 2014 — regarding.

Sir,

Kind attention is invited to this office circular letter No. Actuarial/18(2)
2008/Vol.III/7737 dated 29.08.2014 (placed at SI, No. 401 in the circulars segment
for the year 2014-15 of official website) forwarding therewith a copy of notification
providing increased quantum of monthly pension under EPS, 95. The above referred
amendment will provide a minimum pension of Rs. 1000/- per month in respect of
member and widow(er)/nominee/dependent parents and accordingly the minimum
children & orphan pension will also be increased proportionately to Rs. 250/- and Rs.
750 respectively. It was also informed that necessary changes in the application
software are being carried out and the necessary software shall be released by LS.
Division for release of pension in accordance with the modifications.

2. In this connection, it is informed that the revised software
incorporating the necessary changes has been prepared and the test run is
being carried out. The software is likely to be released very soon. As the
minimum pension as per the modifications made in EPS, 95 will be released
in the BRS processing cycle for the month of September, 2014 (for credit of
pension in October, 2014), you are requested to wait for the circulation of
modified software so that BRS for the month of September, 2014 can be
generated by using the revised application software.

3, In this regard, you are also requested to make necessary arrangements
to give appropriate advice to banks with regard to increase in minimum pension from
the month of September, 2014.

[This issues with the approval of ACC(Hars.)].

Subject:- Filtng of Cases before the Hon’ble High Court against
the order of EPFAT, N.Delhi-regarding.
Sir,

It has came to the notice of Head Office that some of the Hon'ble
High Courts have observed that 7A/148 authority being himself a
judicialfadjudicating authority cannot himself/herself appeal or defend
against the order of EPFAT.

2, The matter was examined with respect to the power delegated to the
officers of the Organisation by the Central Board of Trustees in its 119°”
meeting held on 04.04.1989 and circulated vide letter dated 18.07.2014. A
legal opinion was also obtained in the matter from a Supreme Court Panel
Counsel. It has been observed that:

(i) Writs to be filed by EPFO: The Writs shall be filed in the name of the
Central or State Board as the case may be and the cause title will be as
herein under:

Central Board of Trustees, EPF
Through

RPFC/APFC/Law Official
(Address)

The Resolution passed in minutes of meeting dated 04.04.1989 whereby the
concerned official signing the petition derives his authority to represent the
Board of Trustees shall be mentioned in the petition itself.

(i) Writs instituted by EPFO and pending adjudication: In Writs which
have been instituted by the authorities/officials in their own name and are
pending adjudication before High Court, the counsels to be requested to
move an appropriate application to amend the cause title of the writ sa as to
avoid any adverse order on technical ground.

(iit) Writs instituted by the establishments against the EPFO: In the cases
wherein the writs have been instituted against the authority passing 7A or
14B order and the Board of Trustees have not even been made a party, the
counsels to be requested to raise a preliminary objection that the writ is
liable ta be dismissed on the ground of non-joinder of the necessary party
because as per section 5C the Board has to be sued in its own name.

3. In the light of the above, field offices are advised to meticulously
follow the above direction and take necessary action while filing/defending
the legal matters.

Yours faithfully,

Sub: Furnishing of details required for Assessment and timely declaration
of Productivity Linked Bonus for the year 2013-14.
Sir,
Please refer to the above said subject. The work relating to the assessment
of P.L. Bonus for the year 2013-14 has been taken up by the Headquarters. Ministry
of Labour & Employment vide their letter dated 15th March 2013 instructed EPFO to
review the new PLB Scheme as the 'Productivity Factors' might have changed and
directed to formulate a fresh PLB Scheme and send the same after getting it
recommended from the Executive Committee, EPF. Accordingly, a new PLB Scheme
is being formulated by the National Productivity Council (NPC). As it may take some
time in formulation and getting formal approval of the Central Government, hence it
has been decided to collect the information from all Regions relating to assessment
of P.L. Bonus with reference to existing the P.L.B. Scheme as approved by
Government of India in December, 1999. Information relating to parameters and
performance as per the Scheme is to be furnished, as usual, in the Annexure A to
C (Forms enclosed).
ACCOUNTS & CASH
2.
A time-limit of 30 days (calendar days) has been prescribed for completing
the job relating to settlement of PF, EPS and EDU claims, Transfer cases and cases
pertaining to Advances. In case the job is not completed within 30 days, weightage
would be reduced to half for the work done beyond 30 days. Date of receipt of
claim form (complete in all respect) and the date of dispatch of cheque/transfer
through NEFT would be taken into account for reckoning 30 calendar days. In some
of the cases it was found that the date mentioned on the cheque is taken into
account, which is not correct. The actual dispatch of cheque takes much more time
after the cheque is prepared and signed by the authorized officer. In order to avoid
delay in dispatch it has been decided that only the actual date of dispatch of cheque
as recorded on the slip issued by the post office should only be taken into account.

In other cases where no cheque is to be issued like PPO, Transfer out not involving
actual transfer of PF accumulations etc., the actual date of issue of PPO and the
date of actual transfer will be taken into account.
3.
As regards issue of "Annual Statement of Accounts", it has been classified
into two groups, Viz. (1) current year's Accounts slips issued and (2) Previous year's
Accounts slips issued during the current year. Accounts slips relating to the "current
Year" and those pertaining to previous years but issued during the curren't year
should be shown separately. The Number of accounts slips issued with the help of
outside agencies and the number of accounts slips prepared and issued on
computers of EPFO may also please be furnished separately in Column 9 of
Annexure "A".
4.
Activity "issue of cheque against the PPO of Monthly Pension cases" has been
added in the Bonus scheme, 1999. Those beneficiaries who opt to get Monthly
Pension through their Bank Accounts are sent cheques from the Regional/SubRegional Offices itself. This activity has been included in the PLB Scheme, 1999 with
a view to encourage the staff members to issue the cheques of Monthly Pensions as
promptly as possible. Accordingly, information may be furnished separately for all
the three categories as provided in Annexure-A.
ENFORCEMENT & DAMAGES
5.
The activities of "Enforcement & Damages" include:
(1)
No. of 7A notices issued.
(2)
No. of Speaking Orders of 7 A passed and compliance effected.
(3)
No. of Speaking Orders passed for Levy of Damages.
(4)
No. of Recovery Certificates Executed:-
(a)
For default in all the five Accounts (A/c No. 1,2,10,21 & 22)
(b)
For default in 3 or 4 of the five Accounts.
( c)
For default in 1 or 2 of the five Accounts.
7-A NOTICES
6.
Only one notice has to be taken into account for all the three Schemes. In
case three separate notices are issued for the three Schemes, it has to be taken as
one only. Further, only the initial notice issued has to be taken into account and not
the notices issued every time after adjournment of proceedings due to any reason.
With the amendment of Section 7A, the RPFCs are required to decide not only the
quantum of dues but also to decide the Applicability. In such cases also if more than
one notices are issued, it should be taken as one only for the purpose of PLB return.
SPEAKING ORDERS OF 7A PASSED AND COMPLIANCE EFFECTED
7.
Against this item all the speaking orders passed under Section 7A should not
be shown. Only those orders passed, which have been complied with, should be
shown. However, instructions contained in the preceding para as "7 A Notices"
should also be kept in view.

CAT, Chennai Bench, Chennai.
Sir/Madam,

Sh. Prem Kumar, Sr. SSA of RO, Tambaram has appeared for Departmental
examination for the post of EO/AO during the month of December 2009.

Sh. Prem Kumar, Sr. SSA had applied for re-totaling and verification of marks and the
same was done as provided in the scheme and there is no change in the position in respect of
Sh. Prem Kumar, Sr. SSA.

Being aggrieved by the position Sh. Prem Kumar, Sr. SSA has filed the 0.A No.
1355/2011 in CAT, Chennai Bench, Chennai.

The final hearing heard on 06.03.2014 the Hon’ble CAT Tribunal, Chennai Bench,
Chennai delivered the judgment on 25.03.2014 as follows: -

“We have carefully considered the rival contentions and perused the material on
record.”

“We find that in this case as per rules pertaining to the said examination, the applicant
has already availed the benefit of re-totaling of marks. In the rules notified for the said
examination, there is a clear stipulation that re-evaluation of answer paper is not
permissible in any case under any circumstances. In the absence of any specific rules
permitting re-evaluation of answer scripts, such re-evaluation cannot be permitted and
Courts/Tribunals cannot order re-evaluation in such case. In the light of the above
position, we find that there is no ground in the present case to order such re-evaluation
of answer paper as prayed for in the OA. In the end, the OA being devoid of merit is
liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed with no order as to costs.”

Hence, the O.A is dismissed.

issue of notices, damages and interest levied and amount
recovered is therefore, to be reported by field offices to the Head

excel format only filling up all the columns of the proforma.

required to send the information directly to Head Office. The information
is not to be compiled at Regional Office / Zonal Office level.

No. Budget/44/2014-15/2015-16/Main Dated: 93-07OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Sub: Submission of Revised Estimates for the year 2014-15 and
Budget Estimates for the year 2015-16 in respect of Employees’
Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 (including Employees’ Pension
Scheme, 1995) and Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance
Scheme, 1976.

In accordance with the provisions regarding budget contained in Para 58
of the EPF Scheme 1952, on probable Receipts and Expenditure relating to the
Administration of the Funds, the Revised Estimates for the year 2014-15 and
the Budget Estimates for the year 2015-16 of the EPF Organisation, based on
the actual Income & Expenditure upto 30" September 2014 (i.e. from
1.4.2014 to 30.9.2014), are to be prepared and placed before the Central
Board of Trustees, EPF for the consideration and approval in this financial
year.

2. The budgetary exercise should not be treated as mere routine exercise
and it should receive the personal attention of the Regional P.F.
Commissioner-I and the OIC of SRO for its correctness and timely submission.
On the part of the RPFC-II (F&A), it should be treated as a vital function for
the respective Region including for the SROs and he should devote his
personal attention in assisting the Regional Commissioner in-charge of the
Region. Regional Offices may frame the BE/RE with due care as per provisions
in GFRs after assessing the actual needs of the regions. It has been observed
that in the last five years, RE was more than BE but the actual expenditure
was even less than the BE- this is clearly a reflection of weaknesses in the
budgetary exercise. Further, RE may be projected in such a manner to obviate
the need for re- appropriation in the last quarter of the financial year.

Sub: Gazette Notification providing for increase in wprge ceiling under EPS, 1995 from
Rs.6500/- to Rs.15,000/- which shall come into force on and from the 1° day of Sept.
2014.

Sir,

This is in continuation of this office circular No] Actuary/18(2)2008/ Vol.ITI/5905
dated 23.07.2014 wherein it was informed that the Employees’ Pension Scheme 1995 is
being amended to increase the wage ceiling from Rs.6,400/- per month to Rs.15,000/- per
month in the Employees’ Pension Scheme, 1995.

2. The proposed amendments have since been notified vide Gazette Notification No.
GSR 609 (E) which shall come into force on and from the 1“ day of September, 2014
(Copy of notification enclosed).

3. Accordingly, with effect from the 1° day of Yeptember, 2014, the pensionable
salary for all cases of exit/death on or after 01.09.2014, for calculating pension shall be
the average monthly pay drawn during the contributory period of service in the span of 60
months preceding the date of death/exit from the membership of the Employees’ Pension
Fund. The pensionable salary shall be calculated on|pro-rata basis separately for the
period up to 31.08.2014 up to wage ceiling of Rg.6,500/- per month and for the
subsequent period upto the wage ceiling of Rs.15, 0P0/- per month. Similarly, the
Withdrawal Benefit shall be based on the weighted wages at different wage ceilings. As
already informed necessary amendments in the application software are being carried out

and the necessary software shall be released by I.S. Division at the earliest.

4, Accordingly, requisite steps may be taken so jhat full details of wages for 60
months are available to settle the pension claims im accordance with the proposed
modification. In this regard, Form 10-C & Form 10}D are also being redesigned to
incorporate the above changes and shall be circulated soon. However in the meantime
wage details be obtained by attaching additional sheet for giving details of 60 months of
wages along with Form 10-D in respect of all membgrs having date of exit from EPS
1995.
5. The members having date of exit from}| EPS, 1995 on account of
superannuation/option date for commencement of early pension etc. prior to 01.09.2014
shall get Pensionary benefits on the basis of the existizg pensionable salary calculations
i.e. by taking 12 months average.
6. Further, with effect from 01.09.2014, wherever qmployer & employees have opted
to contribute on salary exceeding Rs.6,500/- per month] such employer & employees will
have to exercise a fresh option to contribute on salary |exceeding Rs.15,000/- per month
subject to the condition that such member would hava to contribute the Government’s
share of contribution @ 1.16% on the salary exceeding Rs.15,000/- per month from his
/her share of contribution. The fresh option is to be exercised within a period of 6 months.
It is essential to know with certainty the employees who are currently permitted to
contribute to EPS on higher wages, so that fresh options can be called for. Accordingly,
you may immediately flag all such cases of contribution on salary exceeding Rs.6,500/-
per month and obtain fresh options in a time bound manner. It may be made known to
the existing optees that if the fresh option is not exercised it shall be deemed that the
employee has not opted in allowing contribution over wage ceiling and the contributions
to Employees Pension Fund made above the wage ceiling in respect of the member shall
be diverted to the Provident Fund account of the member along with interest as declared
under the Employees’ Provident Fund Scheme from time to time.

7. Furthermore, with effect from 01.G¢.2014 the provisions for contribution on higher
salary has been deleted and as such no new options dan be allowed to any member of

EPS, 1995 on and after 01.09.2014.

Notification increasing wage ceiling under the EDLI Scheme, 1976 dated 22-08-2014-Reg.

Sir,

The Gazette Notification issued by the Govt. of India referred above has brought Important
amendments whereby the wage ceiling for EDL! contribution have|been increased from the present
amount of Rs. 6,500/- per month to Rs. 15,000/- per month.

2. Additionally, the benefits under paragraph 22 of this Scheme shall be increased by 20% in addition to
the benefits admissible under Sub-Paragraph (1), (2) & (3) of paragraph 22. The notification will come into
force from 1 September, 2014.

3. With the above amendments in the EDLI Scheme, 1976 the quantum of benefits will be substantially
increased. In order to ensure uniformity in the application of the Anmendments, all offices may note the
following:-

I. In all cases of EDLI claims where the date of death df the member occurs on or after
01.09.2014, the benefits shali be regulated on the basis of the enhanced wage ceiling limit of
Rs. 15,000/- per month alongwith the admissible increase pf 20% under newly introduced Subparagraph (4 Jof paragraph 22.

I. In those cases of EDLI claims where the date of death of member occurs prior to 01.09.2014
the benefits will be regulated on the basis of the wage ceiling limit of Rs. 6,500/- per month.

4. Necessary Amendments in the application software are being made by IS division, but in the
meantime EDLI claims will be regulated as mentioned in the paragraph above. As it is an important
Amendment you are requested to give wide publicity to the same. All Establishments under your
jurisdiction may be advised to ensure compliance under the enhahced wage ceiling. EDLI exempted
establishments may also be informed that benefits have to be paid on the higher wage ceiling along with
20% (Twenty percent) increase in benefits as provided in newly introddced sub-paragraph (4) of Paragraph
22 in all cases of claims where death occurs on or after 01.09.2014. Publicity may be given through press
releases, letters to Employers/Employees Associations, e-mails, regiona| EPFO websites etc.

Subject : Enhancement of wage ceiling from Rs. 6,500 to 15,000 —target and
additional instructions- regarding.

Sir,

Instructions were issued vide this office letter dated 14.07.2014 (placed at SI. No.
268 in the circular segment of the official website for the year, 2014-15 ) and letter dated
01.08.2014 (placed at SI. No. 311 in the circular segment of the official website for the year,
2014-15 ) in connection with the preparatory activities before notification on enhancement in
statutory wage ceiling for enroiment under the EPF & MP Act 1952 to Rs. 15,000/- per
month from the current maximum of Rs. 6,500/- per month. It is expected that the
preparatory activities must have been completed by now to shoulder the challenge.

2. Now Government of India, Ministry of Labour and Employment has issued notification
on enhancement of wage ceiling from existing Rs. 6,500/- to Rs. 15,000/- and the same has
already been uploaded to the web site by this Office circular dated 28.08.2014 (placed at Sl,
No. 388 in the circular segment of the official website for the year, 2014-15).

3. A study was carried out by Ministry of Labour and Employment recently to analyze the
coverage gaps which revealed an alarming picture that a large number of the workforce are
deployed by various Government Departments, Undertakings and Autonomous bodies, both
Central and State on outsourcing basis for activities such as watch-ward, housekeeping,
data-entry etc. to different agencies and contractors and the persons engaged by such
agencies and contractors to execute the above activities. Further majority of the workforce
engaged in this sector are out of the ambit of the Act and thus are not entitled to benefits of
provident fund, pension and insurance being excluded employees. Time has come to ensure
that these so called excluded employees are brought under the purview of the Act which will
help the organization to bridge the coverage gaps to a large extent.

Page 1 of 3

4. Another area where the non-coverage of employees is reportedly widespread, is the
Building and Construction Industry which is labour intensive. Most of the workers engaged in
this industry receive minimum wages which are likely to be much less than Rs. 15,000/.
There is wide scope to increase the coverage base by covering the workers who were not
covered under the ambit of the Act earlier because their wages were more than the
statutory wage ceiling of Rs. 6,500/-.

5. Next in the line is the Placement Agencies which provide manpower to various
agencies, both in Public and Private Sectors, where the concentration of workforce is mare.
A greater part of the workforce reportedly get wages beyond Rs. 6,500/- and thus excluded
and deprived from the benefits envisaged in the Act and the Schemes framed thereunder.
This area needs to be focused to bridge the coverage gap.

6. Similarly, in mines of different nature, deployment of labour force is extensive.
Because the minimum wages, which the labourers engaged in the mines get, being higher
than Rs. 6,500/-, the number of excluded employees are likely to be more in this area. In
view of such enhancement in wage ceiling to Rs. 15,000/-, it is expected that there is
greater scope in covering all such excluded employees.

7. It has also been observed that various Banks, both in public sector and private sector
deploy number of people who draw salary beyond Rs.6,500/- but are not covered either
under the own scheme of the banks or under the Act. These employees are deprived of
Provident Fund benefits. Efforts may be made to explore the possibility of covering all these
employees under the ambit of the Act. It may also be investigated as to whether the security
personnel deployed by the banks in their ATMs throughout the country are getting Provident
Fund and allied benefits or not.

8. In most of the visible establishments like hospitals, diagnostic centers, maternity
centers, hotels, restaurants, schools, workshops, show rooms of branded companies etc.,
the number of workers drawing more than Rs. 6500/- are likely to be sizeable. There is
ample scope for increase in the membership by covering all those employees who draw
salary/wages more than Rs. 6,500/- but less than Rs. 15,000/- under the ambit of the Act.

9. Similarly, franchises and service centers of manufacturers of branded electronic
appliances, DTH Service providers etc. have large number of employees who are not
covered under the ambit of the Act on account of hitherto wage ceiling of Rs. 6,500/-. Now,
since the wage ceiling has been revised, there may be quite sizeable employees who can be
brought under the ambit of the Act who draw salaries/wages between Rs. 6,500/- to Rs.
15,000/- shall be collected by the Enforcement Officer to verify their compliance position.

10. Regional Provident Fund Commissioners, In-Charge of Regional/Sub Regiona! Offices
shali devise appropriate mechanism to cover all the employees working in the covered
establishments but not enrolled as members for the reason that they draw salary Rs. 6,500/-
in view of the present notification of the Government raising the wage ceiling to Rs. 15,000/-
which is effective from 1% September, 2014.

members

also resulted
in the
creation
of a strong
sense
of

portal
and
distributed
to the
various
stakeholders
and in "Update Incomplete Member's Details" after KYC

a daily basis and also for all back periods.
3.
Accordingly,
to
immediately
address
the
serious
Issue
of
shortcomings
in the member
master,

and
urged to be carried out by each field office immediately:
(a)
Upload
and
rewrite
ECRs,
Challan
and
Bank
statements
in the Application Software daily.
(b)
The process involved in new covered establishments

Annexure

Software.

at

Sub.: Officewise sanctioned strength of APFCs - Redistribution — Regarding
Sir/Madam,

Enclosed please find the officewise sanctioned strength of APFCs which has been
redistributed on the basis of following paramaters. :-

i. The number of APFCs for each Zonal Office has been revised from zero to 01 (one).

ii. The minimum number of APFCs in Regional Office has been taken as 03 (three). However,
in respect of Regional Office with less than 1 Lac live subscribers, the number of APFCs has
been taken as 02 (two).

iii. The minimum number of APFCs in a Sub Regional Office has been taken as 02 (two).
However, in respect of Sub Regional Office with less than 50,000 live subscribers, the .
number of APFCs has been taken as 01 (one). ’

iv. The number of APFCs in Zonal Training Institutes has been retained as 01 (one).

2. The allocation of additional APFCs as per the workload has been calculated on the basis of
the following parameters :-

i. The 50% of the total of EPS 95 pensioners has been added to the total number of contributory
members. The sum total is divided by 1.25 Lacs to find out the weightage of contributory
members and pensioners.

ii. Similarly, the total number of establishments in a Regional Office has been divided by 8000
and the total number of establishments in the Sub Regional Office has been divided by 4000
to calculate the weightage of establishments.

ii, Similarly, the percentage of accounts in respective offices has been calculated on the total
sum of accounts of EPFO.

3. In view of the above, it is requested that the redistributed sanctioned strength may be
perused in respect of each office under the respective Zones/ Training Institutes and the
objections/opinions, if any, may be forwarded to the e-mail ID of ACC(Hqrs) ie.
acc.hrm@epfindia.gov.in latest by Ol-Sept;2014. It is further informed that any response
received after the due date and in any other email ID shall not be considered.

Yours faithfully,

Subject: Prompt recovery of current & arrear dues and initiation of
action therefore — reg.

Sir, .
As we are aware, recovery of statutory dues is directly related to service delivery

including settlement of claims and issue of annual accounts thereby reducing the
grievances which may arise, it is hoped that all necessary actions as provided under the
EPF & MP Act, 1952 and IInd Schedule of Income Tax Act, 1961, have been initiated in
respect of each and every RRC under your jurisdiction for recovery of statutory dues.

2. In this regard, the following directions are issued :-

a) Action may be initiated to issue RRCs for the dues assessed only upto 28" of
February by issue of EPF CP-1.

b) All follow up actions as provided u/s. 8B to 8G and IInd Schedule of Income Tax
Act, 1961 may be initiated for prompt recovery of statutory dues.

c) In view of Hon‘ble Supreme Court Judgement in SLP No. 15243/07 and 20736/07
in the matter of Maharashtra State Cooperative Bank Limited vs. Assistant
Provident Fund Commissioner and Ors, (2009) 10 SCC 123 wherein the issue of
priority of dues has been decisively upheld under Section 11(2) of the EPF & MP
Act, 1952, all cases held up in various courts and earmarked as Not Immediately
Realizable (NIR) may be taken up for scrutiny and get them disposed off

favorably so as to ensure speedy recovery of stuck up statutory dues.

d) Cases which are under liquidation may also be taken up for favorable disposal in
view of judgement of Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLP 7642 of 2011 in the matter
of M/s. Esskay Pharmaceuticals Limited wherein relying on the above mentioned
Hon'ble Supreme Court's Judgement, priority under Section 11(2) has been
granted to EPFO even in cases under liquidation,

-|-

i

e) As initiating actions for recovery of statutory dues entails cost / expenditure on
EPFO, it may very strictly be ensured that cost of recovery as circulated vide
circular No, RRC/28(13)03 dated 17.2.2004 for various actions initiated is

recovered in each and every RRC before the file is closed,

3. As per the instructions contained in Head Office circular dated 19.06.2012 (placed
in the @fficial Website of the Organizatiormat SI. Na. 187 of 2012) the targets set in the
area of Recovery of Current Demand and Arrear Demand in Immediately Realizable
Category is 100% and 80% respectively. In order to augment recovery of dues, it has
now beer decided that all Assessing Officers who fail to collect upto 90% of Assessed
dues during the financial year, suitability of such Assessing Officer for continuing in

Compliance work will be reviewed by ACC(Zone).

Sub: -Appointment on Compassionate ground to the post of Social Security
Assistant and Multi Tasking Staff (Gr. C)-regarding

Sir,

The object of the scheme of compassionate appointment is to grant appointment
on Compassionate grounds to a dependent family number of a Government servant
dying in harmness or who is retired on medical grounds, thereby leaving his family in
penury and without any means of livelihood to relieve the family of the Government
servant concerned from financial destitution and to help it get over the emergency.

The application for appointment on compassionate grounds is considered in the
light of the instructions issued from time to time by the Department of Personnel and
Training (Establishment Division) on the subject by a Screening Committee on
compassionate appointment. Accordingly, 88 cases for compassionate appointment to
the post of SSA and MTS were placed before the Screening Committee in its meeting
held on 25/03/2014, 01/04/2014 & 18/06/2014. Out of 88 cases, 57 cases were
recommended by the Committee for appointment to the post of SSA/MTS. In these 57
cases, 19 belated cases and 01 case for appointment of MTS (Trainee) have been sent to
Secretary, Ministry of Labour and Employment seeking approval. Compassionate
Appointment in 37 cases as per list enclosed have been approved by the CPFC. The
vacancy under 5% quota for compassionate appointment on DR vacancy in Group C
(i.e. combined vacancy of Social Security Assistant and Multi Tasking Staff) were
available in Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Himachal Pradesh, Maharashtra, Punjab,
Tamilnadu, Uttaranchal, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal region and 14 candidates
belonging to these regions have been posted in their parent region. Since no vacancies
exist under 5% quota for compassionate appointment in the remaining regions.

Therefore, option from 23 candidates belonging to these regions are being called
through separate letters for their posting in the regions where vacancies are available
under 5% quota for compassionate appointment.

You are further requested to send the proposal in future keeping in view the
vacancies existing under 5% quota for compassionate appointment as mentioned above.

Yours faithfully,

(AMI SINGLA)

Subject: Eligibility criteria for sanction of assurance benefits under EDLI Scheme, 1976 —
clarification
Sir,

References have been received in headquarters seeking clarification as to whether
“Assurance Benefits” under the provisions of the Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance
Scheme, 1976 should be admissible where a member dies after exit from employment
provided his membership to the Fund survives either because he has not preferred his claim
or his claim has not been settled as he continues to be a member in such situations.

2. In this context, the provisions of Para 2.2.1 of the MAP (Chapter 2, Part IV — EDLI
Scheme 1976) which stipulates that ‘the assurance benefit is payable on death of the
member, while in service” have been requested to be re-examined in view of the fact that
retention of membership of the fund is defined in paragraph 26A (1) of the Employees
Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 which stipulates that a member shall continue to be a
member until he withdraws under paragraph 69 of the EPF Scheme the amount standing to
his credit or is covered by a notification of exemption. It should, therefore, follow that
membership of the fund extends till the date of authorization of the payment and there is
no limitation for period of cessation of membership prescribed anywhere in the Act or
Scheme.

3. The issue has been examined and legal opinion has also been taken in this matter.
The legal opinion states that ‘the perusal of the relevant provisions under the EDLI Scheme
shows that the benefit under the Scheme is available to the employee only and merely being
a member of the Fund will not entitle the person to avail benefit under the EDLI Scheme. The
language used by the legislature is clear without any ambiguity. However, whether a person
was employee or not at the relevant time will be a question of fact in each individual case.’

4. The criteria for sanction of assurance benefits under EDLI Scheme, 1976 should be
considered from the perspective of definitions given in paragraph 2(b) and paragraph 22 of
the EDLI scheme. Further, paragraph 2(c) of EDL! stipulates that words and expressions not
defined in the EDLI scheme would have meanings defined in the Act and the Employees’
Provident Funds Scheme, 1952. The “Assurance Benefits” under EDLI Scheme, 1976 is
defined in paragraph 2(b) as underParagraph 2(b} "Assurance benefits" means a payment linked to the average balance
in the Provident Fund Account of an employee, payable to a person belonging to his
family or otherwise entitled to it in the event of death of the employee while being a
member of the Fund.

The ambit of the definition of the term ‘employee’ has to be seen in the context of Section
6C(1) of the Act which defines the purpose for the framing of the EDL! Scheme:

Section 6C. Employees’ Deposit Linked Insurance Scheme. — (1) The Central
Government may, by notification, in the Official Gazette, frame a scheme to be called
the Employees’ Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme for the purpose of providing life
insurance benefits to the employees of any establishment or class of establishment to
which this Act applies.

It is amply clear from the purpose of framing of the EDLI scheme as given in Section 6C(1}
that the scheme is meant for ‘employees of any establishment or class of establishment to
which this Act applies’.

5. As is evident, the EDLI benefits become payable on the fulfilment of the following
three conditions;

(i) event of death;

(ii) person has to be an employee;

{ili} person has to have membership of the Fund

The term “employee” as defined in section 2(f) read in conjunction with Section 6C(1) of the
EPF & MP, Act, 1952 would mean employees engaged in establishments or class of
establishments to which the Act applies. The meaning of “retention of membership” would
be as defined in paragraph 26A of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952.

6. On a composite reading of these provision it would emerge that when a member
dies while in service i.e. in harness, all the three conditions mentioned in the paragraph
above are satisfied and EDLI benefits are payable. However, when the member dies after
leaving employment he/she ceases to be an “employee” as defined in Section 2(f) read in
conjunction with Section 6C(1} of the Act in an establishment covered under the Act, and
thus the third necessary condition for release of EDLI benefits ceases to be in operation and
the benefits would not be admissible.

1.
Sub-Para 7 of Para 36 of the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme, 1952 states as under.
(7) Every employer shall send to the Commissioner
such returns in electronic
fo~mat also, In such form
and manner as may be specified by the Commissioner.
2.
The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation has now embarked upon its next phase of e-govemance reforms
with a view to make its services available to its stakeholders in an efficient, transparent and reliable manner and at low
. costs. In order to make the same successful it is necessary that establishments furnish electronically authenticated
records through the use of Digital Signature (Class 2 and above) while submitting statutory returns, claim forms and other
information requests etc.
.
3.
.
The Information Technology Act, 2000 provides for use of Digital Signatures on the documents submitted in
electronic form in order to ensure their security and authenticity. Digital Signatures facilitate creating legally enforceable
electronic records and eliminate the need to print documents for signing. Digital Signatures provide the following three
features:
i.
Authentication - Digital Signatures are used to authenticate the source of messages. The ownership of a digital
signature key is bound to a specific user lInd thus a valid Signature shows that the message was sent by that
user.
•
ii.
Integrity - Digital Signatures provide assurance to the sender and receiver of a message that the message has
not been altered during transmission.
iii.
Non Repudiation - Digital Signatures ensure that the sender who has signed the information cannot at a later
time deny having signed it.
.
4.
Now, in exercise of powers in accordance with para 36(7) of Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952, it is
directed that establishments covered under the Employees"Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 shall
mandatorily register atleast one Digital Signature Certificate (DSC), Class 2 and above of their employe~s) and for its
authorized Signatory (ies) with the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation as per the following schedule:
..................
...............................•
.
i.
Establishments with more than 50 ECR members - by 30.09.2014.
5.
As regards establishments having less than or equal to 50 ECR members, separate instructions shall be issued
later. However, it will be in the interest of such establishments also to register their DSC as e-govemance mode will
require Their DSCs in near future.

Subject:- Guidelines for Quasi-judicial proceedings under Section 7A of the Employees’
Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952 – regarding

Sir,
Please refer to circulars of even number dated 30.11.2012 and 18.12.2012 on the captioned
subject. The said issue has been reexamined and following revised guidelines are being issued for
quasi-judicial proceedings under Section 7A of the Act.

2.
INITIATION OF INQUIRY - Inquiries should be initiated only after actionable and verifiable
information is placed for consideration of the compliance officers. Following could be the source
information for initiation of enquiries: -
a) A
system
generated
report
of
probable
and/or
actual
defaults
based
on
receipts/remittances position of the establishments. Mapping of individual establishments
regarding the amount remitted as well as the number of employees for whom the
establishment is remitting the dues. (Remittance drop in excess of ₹ 10,000/- and 15%.
Membership drop in excess of 50 members and 15%).
b) Verifiable complaints or information received from general public at large may be another
source for initiation of investigations and/or enquiry.
c) Reports submitted by the Enforcement Officers.

3.
The authorised officer conducting the inquiry shall examine the compliance history of the
establishment viz.:-

a) Amount remitted and the number of employees for whom the establishment is complying.
b) On clicking the number of members, a randomly sorted list of names of members for whom
compliance has been reported by the establishment during the month should be available.
This list shall not contain either the PF account number or the PF balances of the members.

c) Compliance history of the establishments, wherein, details such as pending quasi-judicial
enquiries, pending recovery certificates, pending legal cases in respect of a particular
establishment etc. be made available.

4.
As far as possible the authorised officers shall follow following procedure:-

a) Information received about default will be entered in a Central Register to be maintained
on a central server.
b) On receipt of the information, notice shall be issued to the establishment enclosing the
information on the basis of which the instant notice has been issued. If the establishment
accepts the contents of the notice, then the matter may be verified for further necessary
action.
c) If no response is received then the EO shall be advised to investigate and file a report in the
matter. The investigation report of the EO shall be according to the "Form of Inspection
Report"
as
issued
vide
EPF
headquarters
circular
number
CIII/110001/4/2(25)2014/Hqrs./Web Portal/10398 dated 30-07-2014 (at serial number 307
Office Orders/Circulars - 2014-15).
d) The Compliance branch shall examine the investigation report submitted by the EO and
decide whether any case is made out for initiation of quasi-judicial enquiries.
e) If, on the basis of the report of the EO, it is decided that it is a fit case for initiation of
enquiry under section 7A of the Act, then the report of the EO and observations there on of
the Compliance branch shall be forwarded to the Assessing officer for initiation of an
enquiry under section 7A of the Act.
f) Before recommending any case, the Compliance branch shall specifically verify, whether
any report/record is available on the file indicating the status of the establishment, i,e.
whether it is a closed establishment etc.
g) Complete investigation report should be available on record before initiation of inquiry is
recommended by the Compliance branch. In cases where the complete report is not
received the Compliance branch shall record reasons in writing for initiating the proposal
for the said enquiry.
h) No inquiry shall be initiated unless a prima-facie case exists on the basis of the said report.
i) The Assessing Officers shall, on receipt of the report from Compliance branch open a
separate file for conducting the quasi-judicial enquiry. This file shall start with the issue of
summons for conducting enquiry under section 7A. The enquiry shall be deemed to have
initiated only if proof of service of notice is available on record.
j) The 7A notice shall be accompanied by the documents on the basis of which an enquiry is
proposed to be conducted. A copy of draft notice is attached (Annexure A) for reference.
k) The 7A summons shall be for a specific period i.e. the notice shall not be an open ended
notice and a specific period of default should be compulsorily mentioned in the notice.
l) It should be compulsorily ensured that the legal process of serving of notice as per the Code
of Civil Procedure is followed before any further action is initiated for conducting a formal
enquiry.
m) If during pendency of 7A enquiry further default is noticed, either another summon be
issued to the establishment for extending the period of current 7A enquiry or a fresh 7A
enquiry be initiated.
n) During the enquiry a departmental representative should lead the case of the Department.
This is a legal requirement and is to be compulsorily ensured.

Subject : Inspection of astablishments splitting wages to reduce PF
liability — regarding.

Sir,

The contribution payable by the employer under Employees Provident
Funds Scheme, 1952 is calculated on basic wages, dearness allowance (including
the cash value of any food concession) and retaining ailowance (if any} payable to
each employee to whom the scheme applies. The meaning of basic wages is
defined under Section 2(b) of Employees’ Provident Funds & Miscellaneous
Provisions Act, 1952. Et Includes all emoluments which are earned by an employee
while on duty but excludes the cash value of food concession, dearmmess allawance,
HRA, overtime allowance, bonus, commission or any other similar allowance
payable ta the employee and any presents given by the employer ta his employees.
However, it has been observed that many employers split the total wages payable
to their employees into several allowances in such a way that the said allowances
are covered under the category of exciusians provided under Section 2{b) of the
Act as explained above thereby encouraging the subterfuge of splitting of wages to
exclude the PF liability. Instances have come te the notice where total wages of
employees are splitted by employer to the extent that PF liability is reduced upto
50% of total wages.

Zz. In order to understand the gravity of the issue it has been decided to have ail
those establishments inspected where the emplayers have deducted PF contribution
on fifty percent (or even less) of total wages paid to their employees. So all Officers
In-charge of fieid offices are directed to get such establishments Inspected where
PF contribution has been deducted on fifty percent or less of total wages. The
exercise must be completed by 31.08.2014 and report in the proforma given below
should reach Head Office by 07.09.2014.

Sir,

Please refer to this office circular letter No. Actuarial/ 18(9)2013/14195 dated 06.11.2013
followed with D.O. Setter No. Actuarial/18(9)2013/27479 dated 26.03.2014. As you are aware the time
line for collection of data of more than 95% of active members was fixed as 30" April, 2014 in the Action
Plan for 2014-15 for EPFO.

Earlier, the office-wise progress of collection of ECR member missing details was reviewed on
18.06.2014 and based on review D.O. letters were issued to all ACCs (Political States) highlighting
therein the progress made by the offices under their jurisdiction with request to personally review the
progress achieved by the offices under their jurisdiction.

However, on perusal of the office-wise progress of collection of ECR members missing details as
on 24.07.2014, it is observed that so far only 15 RO/SROs i.e. RO, Jalpaiguri, Mangalore, Nizamabad
and SRO Vapi, Ujjain, Uddipi, Sagar, Naroda, Solapur, Akola, Portblair, Siddipet, Agra, Varanasi,
Gorakhpur have achieved the requisite target of 95%.

The performance of SRO Kolhapur, Lucknow, Rourkela, Kota, Jalandhar, Noida, Goa,
Gulbarga, Warangal, Simoga, Hubli, Raichur, Jangipur, Kozikede, Pondicheri, Vatwa, Howrah
though above 90% is stil] behind target. The remaining field offices are still below the 90% mark in

achieving targets and need more focussed action in this area.

Chennai, Kandiwali, Bandra, Pune and SRO Kukatpalli, Berhampur, Mysore Road, Bommasandra,

special attention by the concerned RPFCs & ACCs so as to achieve the target without cause of further
delay.

the matter personally and advise RO/ SROs offices under your jurisdiction to initiate necessary action for

completion of the task as per the set target immediately without further delay.

Subject : Instructions on Inspection Scheme and new proforma for inspection of
covered un-exempted establishments - regarding.

Sir,

The Employees Provident Funds & Miscellaneous Provisions Act 1952 (Act) is applicable on its
own accord to all the eligible establishments which are statutorily coverable. However, certain other
establishments can enroll voluntarily. For administrative reasons, every establishment is allotted a
registration number (EPF Code number).

2. Once an establishment enrolls under the Act, it is statutorily required to remit dues regularly in
Electronic Challan cum Returns (ECR). It is the duty of PF Inspectorate to ensure that compliance is
regular and complete. The powers for inspection are provided under Section 13 of the Act and can be

exercised by officers of the organization notified as Inspectors by appropriate Government in the
Official Gazette.

3. It has been desired that these inspections should be systematic. The inspectorate staff shouid
not select the companies on their whims and fancies. The methodology of selection should be
transparent and objectively determined.

4. It has been seen that the inspectorate staff need to inspect the establishments in following
cases:

a) Post coverage visit to establishment for collection and verification of documents. This visit
is also used for educating the employer/establishment for compliance under the Act.

b) Periodic inspection at periodic interval to ensure proper compliance as required under the
Act.

c) Inspection as a follow up of a complaint received by the compliance functionaries.

Page 1 of 5

5. In this regard, attention is drawn to the circular dated 26.06.2014 (placed at SI. No. 220 in the
circular segment of the official website for the year, 2014-15) which speaks about the inspection
scheme approved by Hon’ble Chairman, Central Board of Trustees, EPF.

6. Inspections shall be Mandatory and Optional. Mandatory inspection shall be resorted to in the
following contingencies :

a) All new coverage;
b) All establishments registered on ECR portal, not marked as closed and not complying; and
c) Establishments reported for closure.

7. Inspections of establishments other than above shall be based on data and evidence. The
inspection shall be optional in the following contingencies:

a) Remittance drop in excess of Rs. 10,000/- and 15% (weightage of 1:1)[40%]
b) Membership drop in excess of 50 members and 15% (weightage of 1:1)[40%].
c) All other Units [20%].

d) Normally not to be repeated in the same year as far as possible.

For this purpose, the list of establishments will be generated through a computerized system
taking into account the drop in remittance/membership as compared to last quarter.

8. The inspecting officers shall upload the inspection report within three days from the date of
inspection. Inspection will be counted only when the report is uploaded. If it is found that even after
inspection, no report is uploaded, appropriate disciplinary action will be initiated against the erring
Inspector.

9. Taking in to account the above, a simple proforma of inspection has been devised and is
enclosed herewith . The said proforma is mandatory for submitting all inspection reports.

Subject: Modalities for payments out of Inoperative Accounts.
Ref: 1) HO circular No. WSU/Inoperative Accounts/Vol-II/103415 dated 11.03.2011
2) HO circular No. WSU/28(1)2003/Delegation/Vol-II/49436 dated 05.03.2012

Sir,

In the 192nd meeting of the CBT, EPF held on 15.02.2011, following modalities/ procedures
to ensure correct identification and genuineness of the beneficiary alongwith correctness of the
amount for settlement/authorisation of claims out of Inoperative Accounts have been approved: -

a) In all such cases where the establishment is functioning and employer is available, the
attestation of claim forms by the authorized signatory should be mandatory.

b) In those cases where employer is not available to identify the member, the attestation by
the Bank authorities should be insisted alongwith at least one of the documents as
required under KYC (Know Your Customer) towards identity proof (ID) and proof of
residence. These are:

i) PAN Card

ii) Voters Identity Card

ili) Passport

iv) Ration Card

Vv) ESI Identity Card

vi) Copy of electricity/water/landline telephone bill in the name of the claimant
with the present address.

vii) Driving license, if applicable

viii) Any other identity card issued by the Government authority, including
Aadhar Card.

Further, after delegation of financial powers to the Section Supervisor (SS) issued vide HO
circular No. WSU/28(1)2003/Delegations/Vol-II/49436 dated 05.03.2012 (placed at SI. No. 584 on
‘office orders & circulars for 2011-12’ of EPFO website), following changes have been done for
settlement of claims out of inoperative accounts:-

a) In case the settlement amount is upto Rs. 25,000/-, claims will be submitted by DA
(Accounts) and approved by Section Supervisor (Claims).

b) In case the settlement amount is more than Rs. 25,000/- and less than Rs. 50,000/-, the
claims will be submitted by DA (Accounts) and approved by AO (Accounts).

) In case the settlement amount is beyond Rs. 50,000/-, the claims will be submitted by DA

(Accounts) and approved by APFC.

The above instructions shall be followed scrupulously for settlement of claims out of
inoperative accounts. All care shall be taken to reduce the risk of frauds and to ensure that the claims

are authentic and the payments are made to the genuine claimants.

Reference: R-1/C-DAC/2014 dated 21-07-2014.
Sir,
It is hoped that you have already become aware of UAN implementation after
the issue of circular mentioned above. Efforts have been made to further simplify
the same. The complete process has been sub-divided into the following 4 steps:
i) Allotment of UAN to all current contributing members:
This process was to be done by the office of ACC (IS) at Headquarter/central
level. In this regard, UAN stands allocated to all 4.17 crores members who
have made contribution to EPFO in any one of the last 6 months. All these
UAN have been disseminated to respective employers through OTCP Portal.
All the employers can see these numbers.
ii) Dissemination of UAN so allotted to individual contributing members:
The employer is supposed to log on to OTCP Portal to collect the UAN allotted
to his employees and disseminate the same to the individuals. The requisite

printable format containing UAN and other details has also been provided on
the Portal. (This process is to be monitored by respective OICs.)
iii) Seeding of KYC against the UAN allotted to the individual members:
An employer, who maintains a computerized database of each employee
working in his establishment, usually maintains data relating to its KYC namely
ADDHAR/NPR No., Pan Card or Bank Account No etc.
The same can be
seeded through the UAN Portal by sending the text file in pre-defined format
already communicated to them in the User Manual. The KYC data will
automatically be seeded against the UAN of the members upon receipt of this
information.
The employer must give AADHAR/NPR number where ever available and
bank A/c number as part of the KYC detail as it will enable EPFO in future to
provide services directly to the beneficiaries without intermediation of the
employer. It must be impressed upon the employer that little extra effort in
providing AADHAR/NPR and bank A/cas KYC will reduce their effort and cost
considerably in future.
In case, an employer does not have these details, a facility has also been given
to the individual member for uploading the data relating to KYC on UAN
Portal through his individual log in on member portal. The individual is also
expected to upload a scanned copy of his document relied upon for quoting
KYC on the Portal.
The KYC so furnished by the individual will be
automatically captured by UAN database for seeding.
We have set an ambitious target for seeding of KYC which has to be
concluded at the earliest say by 15th September, 2014. The entire process of
seeding has to be monitored regularly by the OIC of respective office.
iv) Verification of the KYC seeded either by employer or by individuals:
The KYC seeded by individuals who have also furnished the scanned copy on
the Portal or the KYC seeded by the employer using bulk facility of seeding by
using text file shall appear as pending task before the employer.

Implementation of National Electronic Fund Transfer(NEFT) for .
payment to EPF Beneficiaries.

The existing arrangement for payment to EPFO beneficiaries is paper based wherein payments are
released through individual account payee cheques or money orders. !t is primarily a manual system involving
considerable time lag between authorization of claim and actua! receipt of payment. This delay mainly occurs

re . ,

on account of:-
i} Lag of many days between authorization of claim and printing of cheques.

ii) Time taken for signing of cheques due to large volumes. : )

iii) Long time taken for physical handing over of cheques and forwarding letter to Speed Post Center,

iv) Very jong time taken by Speed Post Centers.

t as |

This delays leads to generation of huge number of grievances which is a clear indicator of low level of
customer satisfaction. To overcome these in-efficiencies and to curtail the time lag between authorization of
claim and actual receipt of payment, modifications have been carried out in Unix based legacy systern to avail
the electronic route of payment.

Ninety Five banks with over: 67,000 branches are now connected to National Electronic Fund
Transfer(NEFT) network. Payment to these NEFT networked branches are effected six times a day through a
system driven by Reserve Bank of India. FAQ on NEFT is enclosed for ready reference and detailed procedural
guidelines may be accessed at http://rbidocs.rbi. org. in/rdocs/content/pdfs/65253. pdf. Payments to State
Bank of india (SBI) branches are also being effected through electronic route on Core Banking. Solution(CBS)
platform. Day by day a large. number of bank branches are getting connected to NEFT network and only
Cooperative and Rural Banks are now out of the NEFT Grid. Gradually these banks will also be brought on the ,
network but til! such time payments to these banks can be effected through cheque only.

It gives'us pleasure to launch e-payment in EPFO which will enable us to get the benefits credited to
members accounts within 1-2 days of claim authorization, leading to substantial reduction in grievances and
higher customer satisfaction.

Sub: Preparatory action for implementing proposals for enhancing minimum pension
to Rs 1000/-per month and increase in wage ceiling to Rs.15,000/- per month in the
Employees’ Pension Scheme 1995 (EPS)- regarding

se As you may be aware that proposals for enhancing minimum pension to Rs.1000/-
per month and increasing wage ceiling to Rs.t5,000/- per month under Employees Pension
Scheme have been approved by the Central Government. These proposals have been
included in the Union Budget 2014-15 and the Gazette notifications bringing in amendments
to the EPS and other schemes for implementing these proposals are likely to be issued very

soon.

In this regard in order to be prepared for implementing the proposed modifications, you

are requested to take advance preparation actions in major areas in relation to EPS.

1. Change in calculation of pensionable salary:
The proposed amendments in EPS include the fact that the pensionable

salary for calculating pension shall be the average monthly
pay drawn during the contributory period of service in the span of 60 months
preceding the date of exit from the membership of the Employees’ Pension Fund. The
pensionable salary shall be calculated on pro-rata basis for the period upto
the date of Notification where wage ceiling is Rs.6, 500/- and for the subsequent period where
the wage ceiling would be Rs.15, 000/- per month. Similarly, the Withdrawal benefit shall
be based on the weightage of wages at different wage ceilings. Accordingly,

requisite steps are to be taken so that full details of wages for 60 months are available to settle

the pension claims in accordance with the proposed modification. In this regard, Form 10-C
& Form 10-D are also being redesigned to incorporate the above changes and shall be
circulated soon. However in the meantime preparation be made for attaching additional sheet
for giving details of 60 months of wages along with Form 10-D.

2. Option for contribution on higher salary:

The proposed amendments contain a provision that wherever employer & employees
have opted to contribute on salary exceeding Rs.6,500/-,such employer & employees will
have to exercise a fresh option to contribute on salary exceeding Rs.15,000/- per month
subject to the condition that such member would have to contribute the Govt.’s share
contribution @ 1.16% on the salary exceeding Rs.15,000/- from his /her share of contribution.
The fresh option is to be exercised within a period of 6 months. It is essential to know with
certainty the employees who are currently permitted to contribute to EPS on higher wages, so
that fresh options can be called for. Accordingly, you may tmmediately flag all such cases of
contribution on salary exceeding Rs.6,500/- and obtain fresh options in a time bound
manner. [ft may be made known to the existing optees that if the fresh option is not exercised
it shall be deemed that the employee has not opted in allowing contribution over wage ceiling
and the contributions to Employees Pension Fund made above the wage ceiling in respect of
the member shall be diverted to the Provident Fund account of the member along with interest
as declared under the Employees Provident Fund Scheme from time to time. Furthermore, the
proposed amendments would delete the provisions for contribution on higher salary and as

such no options should be allowed in this regard.

3. EPS to apply only to EPF members whose pay at the time of becoming PF member
is not more than Rs.15,000/- per month:

The proposed amendments have a provision whereby only such new PF members shall
become EPS members whose pay at the time of joining will be less than or equal to Rs
15,000/-. Accordingly, the entire employer and employee contribution shall remain in the
Provident Fund and no diversion to EPS shall be made for all new PF members having salary

more than 15,000/- at the time of joining.

Subject:-Conduct of Bhavishyanidhi Adalat — regarding.
Sir,

In a Service Delivery Organization like ours, where our stakeholders are having
numerous expectations from us, the process of Grievance Handling and Resolution
assumes top importance . The Bhavishyanidhi Adalats offer a very effective medium
for resolution of grievances of our stakeholders . They also serve as an interface
between the Organisation and the stakeholders and therefore serves as a platform for
not only speedy and on the spot disposal of grievances but also for eliciting feedback
from the members. Instructions have been issued on the subject of resolving grievances
through Bhavishyanidhi Adalats from time-to-time. However, it appears that this vehicle
for grievance redressal and interaction with the members has not been given the due
importance and seriousness that it deserves.

As such, all field offices are hereby directed to take immediate action on the
following points:-

1) Bhavishyanidhi Adalats must be held on the 10" of every month without fail. If
the said date happens to be a holiday, the Adalat should be held on the next
working date.

2) The Adalat should be held by the RPFC-I/Officer-in-charge and if he/she happens
to be on leave on the date of Adalat, the senior most officer is to hold the same.

3) Details about Bhavishyanidhi Adalats conducted in the field offices should be
placed before members of the regional committees for deliberations whenever
meetings of the regional committees are being conducted in the regional offices.

4) It is necessary that the Bhavishyanidhi Adalat should be held every time in the
RO/SRO premises only .

5) Adequate publicity needs to be given regarding the conduct of Bhavishyanidhi
Adalat. Publicity may be given through regular press releases and

communications addressed to the trade unions/employers’ associations in your
jurisdiction. State Government’s Labour Department should also be intimated
about date of Adalat so that it can also apprise the Trade Unions and other
representative bodies about the holding of such Adalats.

6) Cases registered in advance for Bhavishyanidhi Adalat should be addressed on
top priority and every effort should be made to resolve the grievance before the
date of the Adalat.

7) The cases registered on the day of the Adalat should also be attended to on top
priority and to the extent possible, same day resolution of the grievance should
be the norm. If due to unavoidable reasons, it is not possible to do so, the
position may be appraised to the member and steps taken to redress the
grievance at the earliest possible.

8) All complaints /grievances, by whatever mode, received during the Adalat should
be registered in the EPFiGMS portal. Officer-in-charge shall review the disposal of
cases registered for the Adalat from time to time.

9) Regional office / Sub Regional Office must upload on its Regional EPF website
the positive achievements and extraordinary steps taken, if any, to resolve the
grievance aired during the Adalat on the Regional website of the organisation.

10) A separate section “Bhavishyanidhi Adalat” should be created on the Regional
Website that shall contain the details of Bhavishyanidhi Adalat alongwith details
as mentioned at point (7) above.

11) | Photographs taken during Bhavishyanidhi Adalats should also be sent to Web.
adminisldy for uploading on EPFO’s website.

An action taken’ report in’ this regard may ~be~ sent at
rc.publicity@epfindia.gov.in.

Sub:-Registration of Digital Signature Certificates of the Authorized
Signatories of the Exempted Trusts - Extension of Online Transfer
Claim Portal (OTCP) to facilitate the transfer from exempted to unexempted establishments.

Sir,

In order to extend the Online Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP) launched in October
2013 to facilitate transfer of PF accumulations of members from exempted to unexempted establishments, a functionality for online process has been designed.
The functionality in the portal for online submission of Annexure-K alongwith
Payment Invoice requires digital signatures authentication by the Trusts. For the
purpose, the Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) of authorised signatory of the Trust
is to be registered with EPFO.

2. The process for registration of the DSC of the authorised signatory has been
developed and tested. The process flow for the registration of the authorised
signatory of Trust is same as that of the authorised signatory for the establishment.

The process is explained as below:

(i) The employer would fill up the details of the authorised signatories of the
Trust in the facility provided only to the exempted establishments in the
OTCP portal! in the link “Registration of DSC for Exempted Trusts”
under the tab “Digital Signatures”. The name, designation and mobile
number of the authorised signatories of the Trust would be furnished by
the employer. The employer can then upload the digital certificates of
the authorised signatories of the Trust. The employer can upload the

details of maximum of three authorised signatories.
