A letter (in duplicate) is required to be printed by the employer after
uploading the digital signature of each authorised signatory of the
Trust. The print button given on the same page can be used for the
purpose.

The letter is to be signed by the employer for authorising the
authorised signatories of the Trust for the purpose.

The letter printed for the purpose would also be signed by the
authorised signatories of the Trust in the relevant column. This would
help in the updation of signatures of authorised signatories with the
field offices.

The letter (in duplicate) is to be submitted to the concerned field
offices, where a pending task would be created in the RO/SRO admin
portal (for OTCP). The format of letter is placed at Annexure-A.

The Nodal Officer in each office would receive the letter and would
send the letter (in duplicate) to the respective accounts group for
verification.

The Dealing Assistant in accounts group would verify the signature of
the employer from the office record. He would keep one copy of letter
received from the establishment for its record and for specimen
signature of authorized signatory of the Trust. He would return the
other copy of the letter to the nodal officer after verification and
approval by APFC of accounts group.

On the receipt of above approval of APFC, accounts group, the nodal
officer would approve the pending task in RO/SRO admin portal (for
OTCP) for registration of digital signature of the authorised signatory
of the Trust.

The authorised signatory of the Trust can then use the digital
signature to digitally sign the Payment Invoice for NEFT Transfer of PF
accumulations from exempted establishment to Un-exempted
establishment.

In case the employer wants to revoke the signature of the Authorised
Signatory of the Trust, he will have the option to do so at Ontine
Transfer Claim Portal (OTCP) through EPFO website. On revocation,
the digital signatures of the respective signatory of the Trust would be

Sir(s)

The role of interna) Audit is to tdentify systemic weaknesses/bottlenecks and to help design timely
interventions in order to prevent any loss to the fund hetd in trust on behalf of the subscribers. As per the Mandate

process is audited in [ts entirety. The audit wing was also to ensure the quality of data during the migration from
Manual te Computerized system..

The working of the Audit wing was reviewed and it was felt that there was an urgent need to put in place
systems for the various processes of the audit wing.

Annual Audit Plan

in order to ensure optimal utilization of the audit manpower to achieve organizational objectives it is
important to have an annual audit plan .This plan shall be drawn up Jointly by the FA & CAO and ACC

organization, the main bottlenecks that require special attention, targets set by the organization and any special
needs in view of frauds detected etc.

Sir/Madam,

may be forwarded to this office for onward transmission to Ministry of Labour &
Employment atleast 20 days in advance before the due date, to enable the Ministry to

Reference : Circular dated 02-05-2014 placed at SI. No. 83 of Office Circulars

Sir,

Please refer to the subject cited above. The facility for the establishments to apply
online for the PF Code number was launched by the Hon’ble Union Minister for Labour

and Employment on 30" June 2014. The Portal has been developed with the following
facilities:

A. Options are available for the employer to apply online under the following conditions:

a) Employer of an establishment to which the Act applies and who has not taken a PF
Code number till date.

b) For voluntary coverage of the establishment if the Act is not applicable as on the
date of employer’s application.

c) For any existing establishment, if the employer wishes to have a separate PF Code
number for a branch unit, for administrative convenience.

B. Facility has also been provided for the EPFO Field Offices to record the details
through the RO/SRO Admin Portal to generate the code number after survey of an
establishment where the employer himself has not taken the code number.

C. For the existing establishments facility to fill their Form 5A has been provided
through their login to the ECR Portal. The Form 5A will be later available for
download by the respective PF Offices through the RO/SRO admin portal. For an
establishment applying for a branch code, the filling of the Form 5A will be a pre
condition for the application of the branch code.

Offices will have to enter the online form, there will not be any physica! application form
(hard copy) for the allotment of the code number. However to facilitate error free data
entry, Input Data Sheets for the data entry have also been designed for each type of
application. To help the employers and the EPFO Offices, detailed instructions for each
type of application has also been prepared and they are available from the ECR Portal as
well as the RO/SRO Admin Portal.

3. The online application for the code number will be successful only when the PAN of
the establishment is successfully verified with the name of the establishment as per PAN
through the online facility taken for this purpose. In case of the Proprietorship Firm only
the PAN will be verified both against the Name of the establishment and the name of the
Proprietor mentioned in the Owner’s details. It is therefore very important that the name
should be entered exactly as per the PAN Card. Any error will result in the rejection and
then the employer will have to apply afresh.

ECR Portal and they have been asked to update the PAN of the establishment and the
name as per PAN on the Portal.

5. Post allotment of the code number, and after online confirmation by the State

about the user id and temporary password and will be able to start the remittances
immediately. The details will also be available for download by the respective PF Offices

Sub: Collection and updating Life Certificate of Pensioners under EPS-1995.

Sir,

As you may be aware all pensioners under EPS 1995 are required to submit Life
Certificate/Non remarriage certificate (LC/NRMC) in the month of November every year
through their respective pension disbursement banks. These certificates are required to be
forwarded by the Banks and updated in our application software for ensuring continued
disbursement of pension without any stoppage or breaks and to avoid any undue harassment or
problems for the pensioners.

2. The fact that LC/NRMC updating of more than 11% of pensioners(overall all India
figures) were pending as on date has been a cause of concern. The information on the number of
pensioners and number of LC/NRMC pending for updating were called from offices and it is
observed that a significant number of offices have pendency in excess of 10%.

3. It must be appreciated that concerted action needs to be taken to address this issue. In this
respect the following lines of action/guidelines are suggested for observance by all offices:

(i) All LC/NRMC received from Banks in EPFO offices should be updated in the
application software immediately and without any delay. There should be no
pendency in this area and offices should certify completion of this task.

(ii) Disbursing banks should be asked to forward immediately any LC/NRMC received
by them but not yet sent to EPFO. These must also be entered immediately in the
application software.

(iii) The application software has the facility to generate list of all pending LC/NRMC as
well as for generating individual letters addressed to pensioners. This facility should
be utilized by the offices. Individual letter should be sent to pensioners in all pending
cases.

(iv) | Under the banking agreements for pension disbursement the Banks have the onus for
collecting and forwarding LC/NRMC to EPF offices. The list of pending LC/NRMC
cases generated from application software should be furnished to banks with request
to contact the pensioners at the latest address which is available with them for
obtaining the LC/NRMC.

(v) In the event that death certificate/intimation is received from banks the same should
be entered in the system and pension commenced for next eligible family members.
The PPO file should be verified to ascertain if there are other eligible members but
for whom bank details are not available for releasing pension. They should be
contacted for obtaining bank account numbers for releasing pension. Further, in such
cases if pension has been released/credited beyond the date of death, recovery of such
excess payment should be effected through the banks. If no eligible member exists,
the file should be closed and removed from work load and bank should be asked to
return PPOs in accordance with manual provision.

(vi) There is a possibility that the pensioner has died but family members are not aware
of their entitlements or procedure and have not submitted the Death Certificate either
to Bank or EPFO Office. In such cases the PPO file should be verified and if any
eligible family members are available they should be contacted and informed of their
entitlements and formalities for receiving them.

(vii) Af] open pension cases in the application software for which pension is not being paid
i.e. they are not being included in monthly EPS should be categorized in the format
enclosed and information sent to Headquarter through Zonal ACCs.

All offices may take the above listed actions and furnish the information in the annexed
format to respective Zonal ACCs by 20" July, 2014 along with details of action taken. Zonal

ACCs will monitor the progress as well as compile the information Region wise/office wise in
respect of their Zones and forward to Headquarter by 25"" July, 2014.

Yours faithfully,

years as on the closing date of receipt of applications. The deputation will be
governed as per the instructions issued by the Department of Personnel & Training as

that mere possession of the qualification does not entitle a candidate for appointment
for the aforementioned posts. The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation reserves

the right to reject any application without specifying any reason.

Subject: - Guidelines for dealing with Court Cases-regarding.
Sir,

Ministry of Labour & Employment, Govt. of India issued standard operating
procedure/guidelines for dealing with court cases where Union of India is party(copy
enclosed). On the basis of same, the following guidelines are issued for strict
compliance.

(a) Immediately on receipt of notice/writ petition/application etc., the concerned
officer (RPFC/APFC) shall personally go through the papers and see whether formal
reply/counter affidavit is required to be filed on behalf of Union of India or not.

(b) In all cases, where reply is required to be filed by Ministry, a draft reply will be
prepared on the behalf of Union of India and may be sent to Head Office for sending to
Ministry for approval if required, atleast 15 working days before the last date for filing
the reply before the Hon’ble Court.

(c) The officer concerned will keep track of each court case for taking follow up

action from time to time. The draft reply will be perused and vetted by ‘concerned’ ~ *"

RPFC/OIC before it is forwarded to Head Office for transmission to Ministry of Labour &
Employment for approval.

(d) In case of court orders/judgements, proper analysis of the order etc. shall be
made and the decision to impiement or to challenge the order in the next higher court
shai} be taken in consultation with Ministry if required within stipulated time to avoid
the contempt proceedings in the court.

Sub: Initiation, Reporting & Review of Annual Performance Assessment Reports
(APARs) of Officers and Staff for the year 2013-14 (1.4.2013 to 31.3.2014) - Reg.
Sir,

The nomenclature of Annual Confidential Report (ACR) was modified and
changed to Annual Performance Assessment/ Appraisal Report (APAR) w.e.f. the reporting
year 2008-09. The APAR for the year 2013-14 has already become due :-

2. Reporting/ Reviewing Officer :- The officers and staff have to submit their
resume to the Reporting Officer who in turn will submit the same to the Reviewing Officer in a
time bound manner. A list of Reporting/Reviewing Officers for the incumbents of various
posts of EPFO is given in Annexure-! for reference. As such, the RPFC-I and Officer incharge of SRO are required to draw a list containing name of Reporting and Reviewing Officer
in r/o each cadre. The Reporting and Reviewing Officer be also advised to follow the guidelines
issued by DoPT circular dated 16.02.2009 in the matter of specified schedule date to complete
the writing of APARs. The concern RPFC and Officer In-charge are responsible for completion
of APAR as per schedule enclosed to this circular.

All Group ‘A’ Officer are required to complete APAR with resume in duplicate.
The first copy be submitted to Reporting Officer and second copy of APAR to concern
RPFC/ACC, who in turn forward the 2” copy in r/o all Group ‘A’ officers of zone in one bunch
with list to Head Office for record. It may, however, be noted that the immediate superior
authority who is supervising the work is to act as the Reporting Officer and authority to whom
the Reporting Officer is subordinate is to act as the Reviewing Officer. It is further clarified that
in case the regular incumbent is not in the office to report or review the APAR, as may be the
case, the next level officer in the hierarchy or the controlling officer may report or review the
APAR of the officer as may be applicable. Where only one superior officer is in the channel of
submission, the APAR may be reported and reviewed by the superior officer.

3. Timely Completion of APAR:- The Annual Performance Assessment Report is
the basic management tool available in the Organization to assess the performance of an officer
and staff. The APAR contains vital inputs for considering the matter of confirmation, promotion,

Web Circulation 2013-14

placement in Selection Grade, appointment to deputation posts etc. Hence, the timely
rendering of APARs to the concerned authorities becomes all the more important.

It is, therefore,. requested that all concerned may be advised to strictly comply
with the time table circulated vide H.O letter No. APAR/ 2013/Hars./ 329 dated 03-04-2013 (SI.
No. 9 of 2013-14) in respect of APARs which are due for the year 2013-14.

In case the ACR is not initiated by the Reporting Officer for any reason beyond
30" June of the year in which the financial year ended, he shall forfeit his right to enter any
remarks in the ACR of the officer to be reported upon and he shall submit all ACRs held by him
for reporting to the Reviewing Officer on the next working day. Similarly, the Reviewing Officer
shall also forfeit his right to enter any remarks in the ACR beyond 31* August of the year in
which the financial year ended.

As per the instructions ibid which are to be followed, the Reporting Officer and
the Reviewing Officer are required to complete the APARs as per the schedule. The Reporting
Officer shall have no right to enter any remarks in the APAR after 30" June and the Reviewing
officer shall have no right to enter any remarks in the APAR after 31“ August following the
annual reporting period.

In case the remarks of the Reporting Officer or Reviewing Officer as the case
may be have not been entered in the ACR due to the concerned officer forfeiting his right to
make any entry as per the provision. A certificate to this effect shall be added in his ACR for the
relevant period. In case both the Reporting Officer and Reviewing Officer had forfeited their
rights to enter any remarks, the CR format with the self appraisal given by the officer to be
reported upon will be placed in his ACR dossier.

In this connection the following O.Ms of DOPT on the issue may be referred for
further guidance:-
(i) O.M No. 35014/4/83-Estt.(A) dated 23-09-1985
(ii) O.M No. 21011/02/2009-Estt.(A) dated 16-02-2009
(iii) O.M No. 21011/1/2005-Estt(A) (Pt.I!) dated 23-07-2009

4. Grading of APARs:- Guidelines regarding numerical grading in the APAR have
been issued vide Head office letters dated 14-01-2010 (SI. No. 196 of 2009-10) and further
reiterated vide letter dated 10/11.03.2011 (SI. No. 528 of 2010-11). Separate numerical
gradings have to be given on the assessment of work output, personal attributes and functional
efficiency. These three areas have separate weightage and add upto 100% of the numerical
grading to be obtained by the officer reported upon. Both the reporting and reviewing officer
shall enter the numerical grading in the same table at relevant column. The reporting /reviewing
officer would also sum up the assessment and give a pen picture of the officer reported upon.

5. Where to send the Reports :- The completed APARs for the year under report
are required to be sent in sealed cover to reach the authorities mentioned below by 31* July.
2014 for reporting/review and custody as may be the case. In case of Group ‘A’ Officers, the
officer reported upon may send intimation to the APAR Cell, Headquarters after submission of
resume so that it is followed up by the APAR Cell. Similarly, when the Reporting Officer
completes his/her part of the report and submits the same to the Reviewing Officer for review,
he/she may do so under intimation to APAR Cell, Headquarters in respect of APARs for Group
‘A’ Officers and other cadres controlled centrally or to the Administration/CR Cell of the field
office in respect of other officers/officials, as the case may be. The Regional Offices are also
requested to take such action necessary in respect of Group ‘B’ and ‘C’ posts on priority. The
APARs in respect of EOs/AOs duly reported and reviewed may be kept at the Regional Office
by the respective Regional Provident Fund Commissioner under his custody.

Subject: Computation of reservation for regional cadres - implementation of the
judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court in the matter of Union of India & Anr. Vs
National Federation of Blind & Ors.

Reference: This office letter No. HRM VII/8/1(2010)/JHT/DR dated 23.04.2014

Sir/Madam,

Vide OM no. 36012/24/2009-Estt (Res) dated 20.03.2014 the DoP&T has modified the
para 14 of earlier OM dated 29.12.2005 to the following extent

‘Reservation for persons with disabilities in Group “A” or Group B posts shall be computed
on the basis of total number of vacancies occurring in direct recruitment quota in all the
Group A posts or Group B posts respectively in the cadre”.

The copy of the circular is enclosed. Therefore it is requested to compute the reservation
for persons with disability, however, the following points may be kept in view while computing
reservations :-

(i) Three percent of the vacancies in case of direct recruitment to Group A,B,C and D
shall be reserved for persons with disabilities of which 1% each shall be reserved for
persons suffering from (i) blindness or low vision , (ii) hearing impairment and (iii)
locomotor disability or cerebralpalsy, in the posts identified for each disability. Three
percent of the vacancies in case of promotion to Group D and Group C posts in which
direct recruitment, if any, does not exceed 75% shall be reserved for persons with
disabilities of which 1% each shall be reserved for persons suffering from (i) blindness
or low vision, (ii) hearing impairment and (iti) locomotor disability or cerebral palsy;
in the posts identified for each disability;

(ii) The computation of reservation for persons with disabilities has to be computed in
ease of Group A, B, C and D posts in identical manner viz. "computing 3% reservation
on total number of vacancies in the cadre strength". The Honble Supreme Court has
further directed to compute the number of vacancies available in all the
"establishments" and further identify the posts for disabled persons within a period ,
of three months from 08.10.2013 and implement the same without default.

Sir,
With
a view to simplify
business regulation,
a transparent
Inspection
Policy with
system driven triggers equipped
with relevant
norms and criteria
have been formulated
for
ensuring more accountability,
transparency
and for minimizing
frequent
inspections
of same
unit.
The details
of the
Inspection
Policy as approved
by the
Chairman,
CBT, EPF are
mentioned
below:-
2.
Objective:
The Inspection
Scheme aims to
achieve
the
objective
of simplifying
business regulations
and bring in transparency
and accountability
in labour inspections.
It
envisages objective
criteria for selection of units for inspection.
3.
Criteria of Inspections
a.
Mandatory
inspections:-
1.
In the following
cases, the inspections will be mandatory
for all units:-
i.
All new coverages;
ii.
All establishments
registered on ECRportal, not marked as closed and not complying;
and
iii.
Establishments
reported
for closure.
b.
EPFOwould
set up a Central Analysis and Intelligence
Unit (CAIU) for collecting
and
analysing field level data for a transparent
and accountable
labour inspection
system. The
cases forwarded
through
Central Analysis & Intelligence
Unit (CAIU) of EPFOwill be based on

data and evidence.
EPFO will formulate
an objective
methodology
for selection
criteria of
the cases by the CAIU keeping in view its priorities
and the provisions of ILO C-81.
c.
Optional
inspections:-
In following
cases, the inspections
would be generated
through
computer
using predecided
number
tables taking
into account the drop in remittance/membership
as
compared to last quarter as per following
parameters:-
i.
Remittance
drop in excess of ~ 10,000/- and 15% (weightage
of 1:1)[40%]
ii.
Membership
drop in excess of 50 members and 15% (weightage of 1:1)[40%]
iii.
All other Units [20%]
iv.
Normally
not to be repeated in the same year as far as possible.
4.
Methodology:
i.
Employers to feed master data and periodical returns.
ii.
Inspectors to feed detailed inspection
report.
iii.
Computer
programme
to be provided by NIC taking into account the criteria.
iv.
Computerized
generation
of inspection
programme
and communication
to
the inspecting staff keeping in view the confidentiality
aspects.
5.
General Instructions:
i.
The Inspecting Officer has to maintain
registers of the establishments.
ii.
He has to record the statement
of workers present at the time of inspection.
iii.
In case of contradiction
in the statements
of employer's,
worker
and entries
in the record, the inspecting officer will seize the relevant records.
iv.
Inspection
report
should
always
be
prepared
on
the
work-spot
by the
inspecting officer himself and handover to the employer's
representative.
v.
The inspection
should be carried out during the normal working
hours as far
as possible.
vi.
The inspection
report is being simplified
and under review/revision.
vii.
The inspection
report should be uploaded within
3 days by the inspector.
viii.
In case of violations
by the inspecting staff, entries shall be recorded in APAR.

Sub: Efforts needed to improve monitoring of grievances in field offices of EPFO —Reg.
Sir,

The grievance redressa! mechanism of the Organisation has been in focus in the
recetit past and a number of instructions had been issued in this regard to make the entire system
of grievance more transparent, efficient and effective. We have been able to make impressive
strides in this area and the relatively less number of grievances pending as reflected under
EPFiGMS bears testimony to this. Neveriheless, there is a lot more ground to be traversed. There
is a need to further bring greater customer satisfaction.

In this context, besides reiterating the various directions contained in previous
instructions on the subject, tt is further impressed upon all concerned that ali grievances should
be properly registered on the EPFiGMS system with all details of the member (viz. nature of
grievance, A/c No. contact address, email Id, mobile number etc.) being fed when the EPFiGMS
registration number is allotted, so that system based monitoring of such grievances is possible.

Even after the registration of the grievances of the members, whole hearted efforts
have to be made on priority to ensure that each and every grievance is fully redressed to the full
satisfaction of the concerned member. Action should be promptly taken on all grievances
reflected in CPGRAMS and EPFiGMS systems and replies in this regard should immediately be
provided in the systems to enable Head Office to finally treat such grievances as disposed to the
satisfaction of the complainant. Efforts have to be taken to ensure that the reply being sent or

uploaded is complete in all respects and that there is no room for the complainant to revert to the
office citing the same erievance.

As has already been reiterated in earlier circulars, you are once again advised to
analyse each “Poor” feedback to find out deficiencies in disposing a particular complaint and
take required action to the satisfaction of complainant. In order that member should not feel
dissatisfied against disposal of his registered grievance, efforts need to be taken by you to
invariably use the feedback report as a tool to find out the deficiencies in disposing particular
urievance and more importantly to take appropriate remedial measures with a view to prevent
such grievances from arising in the future, which will in turn result in improved service delivery.

It is also felt that Regional Committees, which play an important role in the Regions in
administering the schemes, are also apprised wn a rewular basis of the grievance redressal
position of the offices. In order to further strengthen the process of monitoring of the grievance
handling machinery in EPFO, it has been decided that there should be a separate agenda item on
grievances for meeting of Regional Committee and a report regarding the performance of the
grievance redressal machinery shall be placed before the Regional Committees, henceforth,
during meetings for members’ perusal and review. Any inputs given by the members during the
meetings regarding systemic improvements or otherwise may be immediately acted upon after
consulting Head Office.

Likewise, data pertaining to Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats shall also be provided to the
Regional Committee for review during their meetings. The data so provided shal| be complete in
all respects and should include and highlight the special and extraordinary steps, if any taken for
grievance redressal. Photographs of Bhavishya Nidhi Adalats held by field offices should
invariably be loaded onto EPFO’s main website as well as websites of Regional Offices.

It has also been decided by the competent authority to constitute a National Level
Committee on Grievances in EPFO under chairmanship of ACC (CSD) with ACC (Compliance)
and RPFC (F&A) in Head Office as members, which shall from time to time review grievance
handling mechanisms in the organization.

(Issued with the approval of Central P.F. Commissioner)

Yours faithfully.

(SK. AGGARWAL) _
ACC (CSD)

AS has been clearly stipulated in the headquarters circular cited first

above no permission will be accorded for contribution on higher wages
to the Employees Pension Scheme, 1995 (EPS) after $.11.2013. As

such, no option for contributing on higher wages to EPS should be

allowed either prospectively or retrospectively in respect of any
member.

The option for contributing to EPS on wages higher than the defined
wage ceiling is permissible only where the conditions as prescribed
under the provisions of the EPS and the Employees’ Provident Fund
Scheme, 1952 (EPFS) are fulfilled. In the normal circumstances the
membership of EPS is restricted to the wage ceiling of Rs. 6,500/-.
The exception of contributing on higher wages is provided in proviso
to Para 11{3) of the EPS. This provision states that the pensionable
salary for determination of pension can be based on the higher salary
‘on the joint request from the employer and employee from the date the
salary exceeds Rs. 6,500/- per month or from 16.11.1995 whichever
is earlier. However, since the contribution to EPS is by diversion of
8.33% of the employer's share of contribution to the Provident Fund
and there is no separate contribution to EPS this option has to be
preceded by an option under Para 26(6) of EPFS duly approved by the
competent authority for contribution of higher wages. Therefore, both
an approved option under Para 26(6) of EPFS and option under

‘proviso to Para 11{3) of EPS must subsist to avail benefits of higher

wages under EPS. In the absence of a joint request both under EPFS
and EPS as brought out above and at the relevant time, the option for
contributing to EPS is not available.

Banks/individual pensioner so that the same is disbursed within a period of 30 days.

administrative action.

Sub:- Medical Reimbursement of full amount to retired EPFO employees - regarding.

An agenda item was placed before the was placed before 55t EC held on 24.07.2006
regarding medical facility for retired employees of EPFO which is reproduced as under:-

“Adoption of CS (MA) Rules, 1944 for extending medical benefits to retired employees of EPFO
and permitting them to avail medical benefits in any central government, state government
hospitals recognized by state government/CGHS/CS (MA) rules as well as Hospitals fully funded
by Central/State Government. The reimbursement to be restricted to the rates fixed by the
Government under CGHS rules/ CS (MA) rules for in-patient Treatment and treatment of
specialized diseases under CS (MA) rules.

The proposal is placed before the Executive Committee CBT, EPF for consideration and approval.
Powers are also proposed to be delegated for reimbursement of medical claims preferred by
pensioners to CPFC, Addl. CPFC, RPFCs in-charge of RO/SRO.”

2. The agenda item was approved by the Executive Committee in its aforesaid 556 meeting.
Accordingly, a circular no. HRM-V/12(2)2004/52960 dated 18.10.2006 was issued, wherein at
Para 3, it was conveyed that,

“The Pensioners as well as their eligible members should have availed indoor treatment in any of
the Central/State Government hospitals and the hospitals recognised by the State/Central
Government/CGHS/CS(MA) Rules as well as hospitals fully funds by Central or State

~~

Government only. The claims shall be regulated for reimbursement subject to the
rates/ceiling, terms and conditions prescribed under the CS (MA) Rules, 1944.

3. It is also important to note that the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, O.M. No.
§.11011/23/2009-CGHS D.II/Hospital Cell (Part III) dated 17.08.2010 stipulates that the
hospitals empanelled under CGHS shall not charge more than the package rate prescribed by
CGHS. The reimbursements were made accordingly.

4. Thereafter various court cases were filed by retired employees of EPFO due to the
restrictions imposed on the reimbursement of the medical claims. Due to the above court cases, a
fresh agenda was placed before the 78th EC meeting held on 5.03.2014 regarding medical
reimbursement of full amount to retired EPFO employees. The 78% Executive Committee
meeting held on 05.03.2014, the EC decided as below:-

“Reimbursement shall be governed as per existing instructions of Government of India.
The atypical cases where payments are being released in compliance with directions of Hon’ble
Courts be complied as reference booklet and similar cases be regulated accordingly.”

5. Accordingly, Para 3 of the circular no. HRM-V12(2)2004/52960 dated 18/10/2006 may be
read as “ The claims shall be regulated for reimbursement subject to the rates/ceiling,
terms and conditions prescribed under the CS (MA) Rules, 1944/CGHS/actual cost,
whoever is lower and as per instructions of Govt. of India.” This is in compliance of the
detailed agenda approved by the 555 EC held on 24.07.2006 in which it was mentioned that the
reimbursement of medical expenditure to the EPF Pensioners shall be restricted at the rates fixed
by the Govt under CGHS Rules/CS (MA) Rules, 1944 of the actual expenditure incurred,
whichever is less. Since we had only issued executive instructions to adopt the CS(MA)Rules and
no notification was issued in official gazette. However, in specific cases, based on distinguishable
facts, a view can be taken on, case to case basis, as per the decisions of different courts in this
regard.

6. In this regard, it may be further added that the Supreme Court in the case of State of
Punjab and others Vs. Ram Lubhaya Bagga while upholding the new policy framed by the State
of Punjab dated 13.02.1995 regarding restricting the reimbursement of medical expenses for
treatment in private hospitals to the rates fixed by the Director, Health and Family Welfare,
Punjab had held that:

“In the Civil Appeals arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 13167/97 and 12418/97, the surgery at Escorts
was after the introduction of the new policy and therefore the extent of medical reimbursement can
be only according to the rates prescribed by AIIMS. However, the respondents there in are not
entitled to the full expenditure that was incurred at Escorts. We therefore, allow the appeals in
part and direct that the respondents are entitled to reimburse only at AIIMS rate.”

Sub: - Forward the proposal for compassionate appointment -regarding.
Sir,

The object of the scheme for compassionate appointment is to grant appointment on
compassionate ground to a dependent family members of the government servant dying in
harness or who is retired on medical grounds, thereby leaving his family in penury and
without any means of livelihood, to relief the family of the government servant concerned
from financial destitution and to help it get over the emergency.

It has come to the notice that some of the regions have forwarded the proposal for
compassionate appointment wherein the death or retirement on medical grounds of a
government servant took place long back which is not with the spirit of scheme. While
considering the cases of compassionate appointment it is should be kept in view that the
concept of compassionate appointment is largely related to the need for immediate
assistance to government servant in order to relieve it from economic distress. It is,
therefore, requested to send all the proposals for compassionate appointment in your region
wherein the death or retirement on medical grounds of a government servant took place
prior to 30/04/2014 within the three days of issue of this letter.

Sub: Issues related to Customer Service - Reg.

Sir,

On review of the grievance redressal position of the Organisation, it has been observed that
while there has been improvement in the rate of grievance redressal of various categories, there is
still a lot left to achieve in the area of customer satisfaction and totally eradicate any sense of
resentment which may arise in the minds of our members, who have very high expectations from us.

It is therefore, imperative to use available mechanisms to control and reduce the level of
members’ grievances in order to ensure that our subscribers/members continue to repose faith and
trust in our organization.

A review of functioning of grievance handling mechanisms in some field offices has revealed
that due to avoidable delays and inactions ,grievances have unnecessarily cropped up and remedial
measures now need to be taken.

Instructions have been issued by Head Office from time to time regarding the procedure for
receipt of claims, their scrutiny and disposal. However, all field office are instructed to pay special
attention to the following issues in their respective offices:-

o,

“ All claims received either by hand or by post in the offices, should be entered in the system
without any delay.

“* — In some cases, delay has been noticed in receiving back claim forms, which are referred to the
Enforcement Officer, for some clarifications/wanting documents etc. This delay should be
avoided.

+,
*¢

Offices should sensitise the employers under their respective jurisdiction to comply with the
provisions of Para 72(5) of the EPF Scheme, 1952, wherein the Employer is duty bound to
forward duly filled in and attested claim application to the respective EPF office within five
days of its receipt. Circular no. CSD-I/ACC(CSD)/Secy./2013/11729 dated 10.12.2013 in this
regard may be referred.

It is observed that often claims are returned/ rejected on minor or flimsy grounds. Objections
in piecemeal should be avoided. In cases of Return/Rejection at the level of Accounts Group,
proper reasons for rejection should be selected in the application software and the general
practice of choosing “Other” option as the reason should be avoided, except in exceptional
cases. The letter for return/rejection of claim should be generated from the system.

Each Office should identify large Establishments submitting claims in bulk and conduct
meetings/workshops, where representatives of these establishments dealing with EPFO
related matters should be invited for discussion. They should be guided about the proper
procedure for filling and filing of various types of claim forms, so that claims complete in all
respect as per the eligibility of the member is received. The common reason/s for
return/rejection should also be discussed to minimize return/rejection ratio.

Seminars, Workshops and Training programmes should also be conducted by field offices for
educating employers and members in consultation with Trade Unions and Employers’
Association to advise them on the benefits available under the Schemes, claim filing and latest
initiatives of EPFO.

Special efforts should be taken to identify such establishments where difficulty in claim
settlements is encountered due to improper maintenance and submission of records by the
establishments. In such cases apart from advising and educating the concerned officer/officials
of all such establishments on the need and importance of filing records and information in
time, the practice of properly updating the records should be well monitored and followed up
and compliance provisions of the Act and Scheme be enforced wherever necessary.

Establishment master should be cleaned-up and be completed in all respect.

All un-encashed and/or time barred cheques should be cancelled and amounts be re-credited
by following due procedure, prescribed for this purpose.

Efforts should be made to trace all such cases where member has failed to receive his claim
settlement amount, where remittance has been made through NEFT mode for various reasons,
such as wrong IFSC code, technical error, wrong bank account no., closed bank account etc.

Further action for re-authorisation of such payments as per prescribed procedure should be
taken without delay.

Sub: Ratio of responsibility and recovery of Over Payments on settlement consequent
upon recent changes in the process/stage of settlement.
Ref: EPFO Head Office Order No. WSU/28(1)2003/delegation/vol.11/108730 dated 26.03.2009

Sir,
Consequent upon the change in the process of settlement of claims from three levels to two

levels and delegation of financial powers to the Section Supervisors in the settlement of claims,
the ratio of responsibility and recovery of overpaid amounts shall be as under:-

The final ratio of responsibility in case of overpayments/irregular payments would be as
under:-

1) Over Payment occurred in settlement of claims, sanction of advances and transfer of
accounts: The ratio of responsibility will be as under:-

a) Dealing Assistant (SSA/SSSA)_ : 70% of the overpaid amount
Section Supervisor (SS) : 30% of the overpaid amount
b) Dealing Assistant (SSA/SSSA) _ : 70% of the overpaid amount
Accounts Officer (AO) : 30% of the overpaid amount
c) Dealing Assistant (SSA/SSSA) _ : 70% of the overpaid amount
Asstt PF Commissioner (APFC) : 30% of the overpaid amount

ii) Over Payment occurred due to irregular compilation of annual accounts/Appendix
°E’ entries. As the approval of annual statement of accounts is a three level process, the
ratio of responsibility will be as under:-

Dealing Assistant (SSA/SSSA) : 70% of the overpaid amount

Section Supervisor (SS) ; 20% of the overpaid amount
Asstt. PF Commissioner (APFC) 10% of the overpaid amount

ill) Over Payment occurred due to erroneous reconciliation in Cash Section: As the
reconciliation is a three level process, the ratio of responsibility will be as foilows:-

Dealing Assistant (SSA/SSSA) : 70% of the overpaid amount
Section Supervisor (SS) : 20% of the overpaid amount
Asstt. PF Commissioner (APFC) ; 10% of the overpaid amount

iv) Over Payment in Pension cases:

a) If the overpayment occurs due to reasons solely attributable to account wing, the ratio of
responsibility may be fixed as follows:

DA (SSA/SSSA) ; 70%
AO (Accounts) ; 30%

b) If the overpayment occurs due to factors solely attributable to pension wing involving two
levels of approval/settlement, the ratio of responsibility may be fixed as follows:

DA (SSA/SSSA) : 70%
APFC (Pension) : 30%

c) If the overpayment occurred in the pension wing, which involve three levels, the ratio of
responsibility may be fixed as follows:

DA (Pension) : 70%
AO/SS (Pension) : 20%
APFC (Pension) : 10%

d) If the overpayments occurred due to reasons attributable to pension and accounts wing
both, the ratio of responsibility will be as follows:

(1) In case the settlement/approval involves two levels in Pension wing
DA (Accounts) : 35%
AO(Accounts) 15%
DA (Pension : 35%
APFC (Pension) : 15%

(ii) In case the settlement/approval involves two levels in Pension wing

DA (Accounts) L 35%
AO (Accounts) : 15%
DA (Pension) : 35%
SS/AO (Pension) ‘ 10%

APFC (Pension) : 05%

Subject: Special Recovery Drive during the month of August, 2014.
Sir,

The increasing trend of arrears of Provident Fund and allied dues has become a
matter of great concern. So much so, the performance in recovery of current and arrear dues
is far below the targets fixed by the Headquarters which is not at all appreciable.

2. The all India Performance for the year ending 31.03.2014 as per Annual
Business Pian shows poor performance of recovery which js not acceptable and which is a
matter of great concem,

3. In order to augment recovery, it has been decided that a Special Recovery Drives shall
be carried out at regular intervals. The first of such drive shall be in the month of August, 2014
(for both un-exempted and exempted sector).

4. Instructions (Issued vide this office letter dated, 19.06.2012 (placed at S. No. 187 at
website), 13.07.2012 (placed at S. No. 221 at website) and dated 01.10.2013 (placed at S.
No. 411 at website) should be adhered to scrupulously.

5. The following points shail be kept in mind while conducting the Special Recovery
Drive:

a) Maximum number of Enforcement Officers, as far as practicable, shall be
detailed to carry out such drive without disturbing other functional areas.
The Enforcement Officers before proceeding in the matter shall gather all
information viz. details of bank accounts, details of sundry debtors etc. from
the records available in the office and also from third party source like
Income Tax Department, Inspector of Factories and Boilers’, Inspector of
Shops and Establishments, Employees’ State Insurance Corporation,
Regional Transport Authorities, Industries and Commerce Departments,
Industrial Estates, Local Bodies, Co-operative Department, Director of
Mining and Geology, Employers’ Associations, Trade Unions etc.

b) RPFCs, In-charge of Regional Offices/Sub Regional Offices shall monitor the
progress of recovery during the currency of the drive on weekly basis and action
plan accordingly shall be prepared for the following week(s). Necessary action
against non-performing Officers/Officials shail be initiated and informed to
Headquarters.

c} Vide publicity shall be given on such launching of the Specia) Recovery
Drive through local News Paper, display on the notice boards of the Office
prominently, through Employers’ Associations and Trade Unions.

d)} The performance of the Regional Office during the drive in recovery of current
and arrear dues must be reported office wise by the ACCs of the zone in the
Annexures enclosed for un-exempted and exempted sectors separately to Head
Office on a weekly basis with the report of the week to be received in Head Office on
every Friday by 5.30 PM by e-mail at dir,recovery@epfindia.gov.in, The consolidated
report for the month must be received in Head Office by 05.09.2014 without fail.

€) Reports received from Regional Offices and Sub Regional Offices will not
be taken in to cognizance.

f) It shall be noted that the amount outstanding as on 01.08.2014 shall be
the Opening Balance and recoveries made prior to 01.08.2014 shall not be
Included with recoveries made during the recovery month,

g) It is further clarified that the figures reported during recovery month must
be the sarne as reported in ABP report which will be the monitoring report for
the performance of recovery.

6, The above actions are meant to be taken for meeting the objectives of
speedy recovery of dues and not for any harassment of the ermployers/
defaulters, which the RPFCs must ensure.

7, It is hoped that all out efforts shall be made to make the Special Recovery
Drive a success in Its true spirit. Any laxity shall be dealt strongly,

(This Issues with the approval of CPFC)
Yours faithfully,

Subject : Timely action in Contempt Cases.
Sir,

The law of contempt of court has, as its sole purpose, the maintenance of the authority and the dignity of
the courts. Supreme Court, the Court of Appeal and the High Courts have power to punish persons for contempt of
court in accordance with the law. Jurisdiction for contempt of court exists in a limited form under statute and generally,
under common law.

2. Acontempt case generally originates from non-compliance of orders of the Hon'ble Courts. Broadly, the following
are the reasons for being held in contempt of court :

a) Being disrespectful to judge.

b) Not obeying a lawful court order handed down by a judge.

c) Disruption of tegal proceedings by poor behaviour.

d) Publication of material that can jeopardize someone getting a fair trial.

3. There are two types of contempt - criminal and civil. Criminal contempt occurs when the contemnor actually
interferes with the ability of the court to function properly - for example, by yelling at the judge. This is also called direct
contempt because it occurs directly in front of the judge. Civil contempt occurs when the contemnor wilfully disobeys a
court order. This is also called indirect contempt because it occurs outside the judge's immediate realm and evidence
must be presented to the judge to prove the contempt.

4. _ Instructions have been issued in past to handle the contempt cases properly. Further, in record notes of various
review meeting of Zones and Regional/Sub Regional Offices, it was instructed to file reply to all court cases invariably
within one month or within the time allowed by the court, whichever is earlier, without fail, On the contrary, it is
observed that replies are not filed within the stipulated time. Various High Courts take objection to this and pass
strictures. Even sometimes, High Courts declare the defiant person (called the contemnor) in contempt of court.

5. _ In view of above, in supersession of all instructions issued in this regard, the field offices are directed to adhere to
the following instructions in all contempt cases:

a) Wherever contempt notices are received and where Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)/Central
Provident Fund Commissioner (CPFC)/Central Board of Trustees (CBTVUnion of India (UOl) are
respondents, RPFCs-In-Charge of Regional and Sub Regional Offices shall promptly inform Head Office
within 24 hours and that too in e-mail.

b) The draft reply on behalf of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)/Central Provident Fund
Commissioner (CPFC)/Central Board of Trustees (CBT)/Union of India (UOl) to the contempt notices shal! be
forwarded to Head Office within next 48 hours and that too in e-mail detailing therein the Act and Scheme
provisions for vetting at Head Office through Additional CPFC (Zones).

c) In cases, where contempt of court is ordered requiring compliance by Employees’ Provident Fund
Organisation (EPFO)Central Provident Fund Commissioner (CPFC)/Central Board of Trustees (CBT)/Union
of India (UOI), RPFCs-In-Charge of Regional and Sub Regional Offices shall promptly inform Head Office
within 24 hours and that too in e-mail.

d) The draft replies to the contempt orders shall be brought to the notice off Head Office within next 48 hours
alongwith justification, whether to comply or file appeal against such order and legal opinion through
Additional CPFCs(Zones) along with their comments in next 48 hours and that too in e-mail.

e) On receipt of the draft reply from field offices, both for contempt notices and for contempt orders, the Legal
Cell at Head Office shall bring it to the notice of CPFC and forward a copy of the draft reply to the concerned
division for vetting within 2 days of receipt from the receipt of the reply from field offices.

f} The concemed divisions at Head Office shall vet the draft reply and forward to Legal Cell within next 2 days of
receipt.

g) The Legal Cell on receipt of the vetted reply from the concerned division/s shall forward the reply so vetted to
the respective field offices for immediate filing of reply in the appropriate court within next 2 days and that too
in e-mail.

h) Wherever Union of India is a respondent, an application requesting exemption from persona! presence on
behalf of Secretary (Labour and Employment) shall be immediately filed by the respective field offices.

i) The orders of the Hon'ble High Courts shail be dealt with due diligence and due respect. Under no
circumstances, the orders of the Courts be flouted as disobedience to the orders of the Court result in
contempt of Court and creates embarrassment for the higher authorities.

6. Ministry of Labour and Employment has also prescribed a proforma for sending a monthly report on contempt
cases which requires to be submitted by the 2% of every month to Head Office for compilation and onward
transmission to Ministry. The said proforma has already been circulated to field offices. However, a copy of the same is
attached herewith for ready reference.

7. Central Provident Fund Commissioner has further directed that any violation of these instructions will be the
personal responsibility of the Officer-in-Charge of the contempt petition.

(This issues with the approval of the Central Provident Fund Commissioner.)

Subject: Timely implementation of the orders of various Courts.

Sir,

It has come to the notice of Head Office that orders passed by various legal
fora remain unattended. Had Office is informed at the last moment only when the
time prescribed for complying with the order is almost over. It has been viewed
seriously by Central Provident Fund Commissioner.

2. Wherever Central Provident Fund Commissioner or Union of India are
respondents and orders are passed by Hon’‘ble Courts for compliance with specific
direction which are time bound, it must be brought to the notice of Head Office
same day by fax and email. The concerned divisional head at the Head Office
should also be informed telephonically by the Regional P.F. Commissioner/Officer
in-charge of the Regional Office/Sub Regional Office. The order of the court should
also be forwarded immediately to know the exact content and details of the order
alongwith brief history and fact of the case.

3. It has also been reported that the delay in noticing of the order of the court
is due to lack of proper watch and monitoring of the cases and their development
or due to non checking of the position of the cases from the website of the
concerned courts. It might be also further due to negligence of the panel advocates
in intimating the orders in time.

4, In either of the case it is the responsibility of the concerned officer in charge

to inform Head Office immediately with a detailed report in the matter through
Addl. Central P.F. Commissioner (Zone).

5. These instructions are to be followed strictly by all concerned.

Subject : Proper handling of legal cases in field offices-regarding.
Sir,

A number of circulars were issued in past containing instructions on handling of
legal cases of EPFO at various courts. Even then, it is observed that no proper attention is
generally given to legal cases and this area of work has remained neglected over the
years.

2. Very often the work related to legal matters in field offices are handled by the
lower functionaries, may it be an administrative issue or a compliance issue or a pension
issue or a finance issue. Officers in charge of the various divisions are not getting
themselves involved and allow the same to go as like that only. They fail to bestow their
personal attention. The para-wise comments prepared by the lower functionaries are not
properly scrutinized and sent to the advocate in a routine and casual manner. Many a
time, para-wise comments do not contain important points and are found to be
incomplete and inappropriate. Even those suffer from conceptual fallacy. The panel
advocates are not properly briefed and timely instructions are not given to them. As a
result most of the cases are adjudicated against the department by issue of adverse
orders, strictures, observation on the functioning of the organisation and sometimes even
result in imposition of costs also by the Hon’ble Courts. Consequently, reviews and
appeals filed before higher judicial forum and Appellate Authority rarely succeed and
organisation is stuck with unfavourable orders. The adverse orders have long term
implication and ramification for the organisation combined with financial repercussions in
many of the matters.

3. As legal matters impact the functioning of the organisation and stake-holders, it is

imperative that these ought to be handled with utmost care and responsibility by all
concerned.

4. Keeping that in view, it is thought proper to issue some guidelines for improving
the manner in which the legal cases are dealt at present. Accordingly, the following
guidelines are issued for proper handling of legal cases before various courts

a) Meticulous handling of cases at their original level:

It is a fact that any legal case has the best chance of succeeding at the first stage
of litigation. Contrary to that, very little attention is accorded to the cases at the levels of
original trial i.e. at the District Consumer Forum, Lower courts, EPFAT etc. resulting in
adverse decisions. These adverse orders rarely get reversed in spite of being dragged up
to the level of the Supreme Court. This is so because the infirmities set in at the ingeption
of the case get perpetuated at the appellate levels. For example, facts not submitted at
the initial trial level are not allowed to be brought in at the appellate stages. Thus, even
with the best of efforts later on, it becomes hardly successful to convince the court at
appeal level. Therefore, it should be our endeavour to succeed at the initial level of trial
itself instead of depending on appeals to repair the damage suffered at the initial stages.
The Regional PF Commissioners-In-Charge of Regional/Sub Regional Offices shal! ensure
that the cases are sincerely defended at the original levels through an effective counsel
or an Enforcement Officer depending upon the requirement of the case. This is the most
important step towards defending a legal matter and should be scrupulously followed. It
may also be ensured that proper para-wise comments are sent to the advocates and
counter replies are prepared duly incorporating the facts and provisions of the Act and
the Schemes. Advocates are briefed properly by the concerned officer whose action
/order is challenged or is the subject matter of litigation without shifting the onus on the
officials posted in the legal cell. An entry to this effect shall invariably be made in the
legal file as well as in the file of concerned section so that the advocate could be asked in
case the matter is not argued as per briefing. It may be noted that losing a case at the
original level shall reflect negatively against the performance of the concerned
Officer/Officer-In-Charge.

b) Timely filing of Counter Reply:

Timely filing of counter reply is an important step towards disposal of legal cases.
Due to non-filing of counter affidavits, the cases are pending before different courts for
long period of time with stay granted on statutory actions. In many of the cases, the
assessment is held up or recovery action is stayed by the Courts. By the time the |case is
disposed of, the employees who were eligible for the benefits leave the establishment,
become untraceable or even expire .The establishments claim to have no details of their
whereabouts. Hence, the whole purpose and the mandate of Act are defeated due to
delayed disposal! of legal cases. In order to expedite early disposal! of cases, counter
affidavits shall be filed within the time stipulated by the Courts or within one month of
the order, whichever is earlier without fail and no extension of time should be sought.
Additional CPFCs (Zones) and RPFCs must scrutinise such files where delayed counters
are filed and fix responsibility on the erring officials.

Subject : Guidelines on rate of surcharge to be levied on Board of Trustees of the
exempted /relaxed establishments on account of deviation from the prescribed
pattern of investment by RPFCs.

Sir,

Exemption from the implementation of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 is granted
to an establishment under the provisions contained in Section 17(1)(a) and Section 17(2) of the
Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 read with Para 27A of the
Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952. Further, provisions contained in Paragraph 79 of the
Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 provides for grant of relaxation pending the disposal of the
establishment's application for grant of exemption under Section 17 of the Act.

2. Paragraph 27AA of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 provides that all exemptions
already granted or to be granted hereafter under Section 17 of the Act or under Para 27A of the Scheme
Shall be subject to the terms and conditions as given ion the Appendix - A.

3. Section 17(1A)(b) of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952
stipulates that where an exemption has been granted to an establishment under clause a of sub-section
1, the employer shall establish a Board of Trustees for the administration of the Provident Fund. Section
17(1A)(d)(iii) provides that the Board of Trustees so constituted shall invest the Provident Fund monies
in accordance with the direction issued by the Central Government from time to time.

4. Further, Paragraph 27AA of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 provides that all
exemptions already granted or to be granted hereafter under Section 17 of the Act or under Paragraph
27A of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 shall be subject to the terms and conditions as

given in the Appendix - ‘A’. Condition No. 17 of Appendix — ‘A’ to Paragraph 27AA of the Employees’
Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 stipulates that:

“The Board of Trustees shall invest the monies of the provident fund as per the directions of the
Government from time to time. Failure to make investments as per directions of the Government
shall make the Board of Trustees separately and liable to surcharge as may be imposed by the
Central Provident Fund Commissioner or his representative.”

Page 1 of 4

5. Central Government (Ministry of Labour & Employment) notifies the pattern of investment from
time to time. The latest notification relating to pattern of investment is that which was issued under S.O.
2126 dated 9" July, 2003 published in the Gazette of India, Pt — II, Section — 3 (ii) vide Issue No. 30
dated 20-26" July, 2003.

6. Till date, guidelines on levy of surcharge in case of default on this count by Board of Trustees of
exempted/relaxed establishments have not been finalised. It has been the experience of EPFO that
Board of Trustees of exempted/relaxed establishments have many a times failed to adhere to the
notified pattern of investment for one reason or the other. Though, the annual inspections are required
to be done by the Inspectors of the Provident Fund Office but these inspections are not being done
regularly. Sometimes, the inspections of the exempted establishments have not been carried out even
once during the year.

7. Extensive discussions with the stakeholders have been made during the year, 2013-14 regarding
the way the exempted Trusts are functioning. Though the issue of surcharge so called fine was not
raised specifically, it was felt by the exempted Trusts that levy of surcharge with retrospective effect
may not be advisable. Therefore, surcharge, if any, being imposed for deviation in adherence to the
pattern in earlier years may be kept minimal.

8. The issue of levy of surcharge and its rates was placed before the Sub-Committee of Central
Board of Trustees, EPF on Exempted Establishments in its 35" meeting held on 28" March, 2014 for
decision on the following issues:

a) rates of surcharge to be levied on Board of Trustees for deviation in the investment pattern
prescribed and
b) extent of deviation.

Subject: Responsibility Mapping and Streamlining the Grievance Redressal Mechanism — reg
Sir,

Redressal of grievances is one of the primary responsibilities of a service oriented organisation
such as EPFO and need to have a responsive and efficient redressal mechanism is Imperative, EPP Internet
based Grievance Management System (EPFGMS) was introduced a few years back for speedy and effective
resolution of grievances. It also has the added facility of online monitoring of arievances and to oversee the
overall quality and periodicity of their disposal. The recent months have seen a renewed emphasis from
various quarters on the subject of grievance redressal by the organisation, It is necessary that monitoring of
grievances needs to be done ona continuous manner so as to bring down the pendency and to ensure that
bur stakeholders’ interests are taken care of and their concerns addressed by the organization.

Tt is felt necessary that the entire protocol, starting from the registration of grievance to its final
disposal and further systematic corrective action taken by the concerned field office are followed in its
entirety in order to achieve the desired results, For effective monitoring of the receipt and disposal of
grievances; it has been decided that each office shall appoint officer(s) as nodal officer, not below the rank
of AO. In case of offices with high number of subscribers or inflow of grievances, there can even be more
than one officer designated as Nodal Officer, The nomination of Nodal Officer shall be done by the Officerin-Charge of each field office.

In order to further streamline the entire process of grievance redressal monitoring and disposal, it
is felt necessary that responsibility chart be prepared and activated in all the field offices so that every
grievance is taken seriously and non-attendance of the grievance results into action against the defaulting
officer / official. Grievance should go through the various stages such as registration, marking the
grievance to the relevant section, its disposal, evaluation of feed-back etc.

1. Receipt of grievance and its registration: First and foremost attention should be given to
the registration of grievance on the EPFIGMS portal. While there is an Increase in the
tendency on the part of members to directly register their grievance on the EPFIGMS portal
which is welcome, there are still a sizeable chunk of grievances received by traditional means
such as post, fax, telephone, e-mail, in person etc., which need to be compulsorily registered
in the EPFIGMS for which Instructions have already been issued vide letter No.

MIS/3( 1L)RFO/MOLAE/2013-14 dated 08.07.2013 and reiterated In the Review Meeting of ACCS
dated 06.09.2013. Customer Service Division of each field office shal! ensure that no grievance
is left unregistered in the system, The process of receipt and registration of grievances should
be completed within two working days. The grievances received in physical form elther by
post in the receipt section or in person in the office of received through e-mail, fax, telephone
or any other means should be forwarded to the local CSD within one day. CSD should
register all the grievances received by any mode in EPFIGMS within one day. While
registering grievances in EPFIGMS, CSD section should ensure that the details of complainant
like address, mobile number, email, if any and nature of grievance is entered in the System,
Letter of the complainant and other documents submitted, if any should be scanned and
Uploaded while registering the grievance. The responsibility to register grievance in EPRIGMS
les with the SSA/SS5A/55 of CSD. The nodal officers must see the DAK register and also
remain in touch with the PRO to ascertain that all the grievances received In the office are
entered in the EPFIGMS system. Nodal Officer will be overall responsible for timely registration
of grievances,

Marking of grievance to the relevant section/branch: It is very Important in the
grievance redressal mechanism that when the complaint is received, it should be handed over
to the person who is supposed to redress it. The nodal officer shall closely monitor forwarding
of grievance to the concemed section and he/she will be held responsible for any laxity.
However, in case the nodal officer finds a problem in forwarding of grievance, he/she should
obtain orders fram the Officer in Charge of the RO/SRO as to whom the grievance belongs to.
It is expected that forwarding the complaint to the relevant official should not take more than
one working day and (n case of any confusion, not more than three days.

Reply from concerned section after resolution of the grievance: The concerned branch
officer should meticulously examine the grievance and take all efforts for disposal. In case any
information/clarification Is required from the complainant, the same may be obtained,
preferably aver telephone. The action taken on grievance alongwith details of disposal should
be communicated to the local CSD within three days from the date of receipt of grievance
from €SD. In some complicated complaints time taken should not be more than seven
days, but It should be in the knowledge of RPFC-I/OIC.

Evaluation of reply by CSD: The reply recelved from the branch officer should be evaluated
by CSO section within two days from the date of receipt of reply from the concemed branch
officer, In case the nodal officer is not satisfied with the reply received from the concerned
branch officer, he/she shall seek clarification from the Branch officer. If required, the matter
can also be brought to the notice of RPFC-IL (CSD) in RO /RPFC-I in-charge of SRO, RPFC-1's
intervention may also be sought if need arises.

Uploading reply onto EPFIGMS portal; Overall responsibility for this task lies with the
nodal officer. The reply received and evaluated should be uploaded on the grievance portal
within one day from the date of approval by the nodal officer. In case final reply Is not
possible then interim reply must be uploaded and efforts should be continued for final disposal
expeditiously,

Reply to complainant: In case of grievances received in offline mode where emall/phone
number is not mentioned by the member, the disposal of grievance should be communicated
to the member/complainant through speed-post within ome day, besides uploading reply on
the portal. The nodal officer shal) monitor this task on regular basis. While communicating the
response to the complainant, the Nodal Officer shall also mention that |f the complainant is not
satisfied with the reply or response given, he/she can approach the Officer-in-Charge also.
Evaluation of feedback from complainants: For maintaining the quality of disposal, the
nodal officer shall make use of feedback given by complainants in EPFIGMS. Wherever the
response is rated as “poor” in the feedback, he/she shall examine each individual case
separately and find out the reasons for the unsatisfactory response from the office, If It is

Sir
Sub-para (2) of Para 36 along with Para 61 of the Employees' Provident
Fund
Scheme 1952 mandates that
the employers at monthly intervals,
shall furnish
Form
5, along with nominations
in Form 2 in respect
of employees qualifying
to become
members of the Fund for the first
time. Further,
the employers are also mandated
to specify through a return,
as may be specified
by the Commissioner, the employees
leaving service.
2.
It
has been observed that
even though this is a mandatory
requirement,
it is
not getting
enforced
uniformly
across locations and lor establishments.
During the
review meetings
held earlier
this
aspect
has been repeatedly
emphasized
and it
should have been part of regular review of Enforcement
Officers.
You may confirm
whether
the same was done and if so the outcome of such a review. You may also
confirm the action taken against non-performing
EOs in this regard.
3.
The updation of members' record
is an essential activity
impacting wide range
of operations of EPFO. It
is accordingly directed
that henceforth
it shall be ensured
that
as mandated
in sub para (2) of Para 36 of
EPF Scheme, complete
member
records
of all members
in respect
of whom contributions
have been remitted
in
previous month shall be mandatorily
collected
by field
offices.
4.
An essential
part of updation of member records
is enforcement
of para 34
of the EPFScheme 1952, which mandates that if an employee joins an establishment,

the employer of the establishments
shall obtain and furnish
to the Commissioner
details of his/her
past membership of the "Fund". This is also a mandatory activity
and is very important
especially in view of impending launch of the Universal Account
Number (UAN) for all members of the "Fund".

Sir,

Exemption from the implementation of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 is
granted to an establishment under the provisions contained in Section 17(1)(a) and Section
17(2) of the Employees’ Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 read with
Paragraph 27A of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952. Further, provisions contained
in Paragraph 79 of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 provides for grant of

relaxation pending the disposal of the establishment's application for grant of exemption under
Section 17 of the Act.

2. Paragraph 27AA of the Employees’ Provident Funds Scheme, 1952 provides that all
exemptions already granted or to be granted hereafter under Section 17 of the Act or under

Paragraph 27A of the Scheme shall be subject to the terms and conditions as given in the
Appendix - A.

3. Condition No. 24(a) of Appendix - A to Paragraph 27AA of the Employees’ Provident
Funds Scheme, 1952 stipulates that:

"The account of the Provident Fund maintained by the Board of Trustees shall be subject to
audit by a qualified independent chartered accountant annually. Where considered
necessary, the CPFC or the RPFC in-charge of the Region shall have the right to have the

accounts reaudited by any other qualified auditor and the expenses so incurred shall be
borne by the employer.”

Subject: Computation of reservation for regional cadres - implementation of the
judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court in the matter of Union of India & Anr. Vs
National Federation of Blind & Ors.

Sir/Madam,

Vide OM no. 36012/24/2009-Estt (Res) dated 20.03.2014 the DoP&T has modified the
para 14 of earlier OM dated 29.12.2005 to the following extent

“Reservation for persons with disabilities in Group “A” or Group B posts shall be computed
on the basis of total number of vacancies occurring in direct recruitment quota in all the
Group A posts or Group B posts respectively in the cadre”.

The copy of the circular is enclosed. Therefore it is requested to compute the reservation
for persons with disability, however, the following points may be kept in view while computing
reservations :-

(i) Three percent of the vacancies in case of direct recruitment to Group A,B,C and D
shall be reserved for persons with disabilities of which 1% each shall be reserved for
persons suffering from (i) blindness or low vision , (ti) hearing impairment and (iii)
locomotor disability or cerebralpalsy; in the posts identified for each disability. Three
percent of the vacancies in case of promotion to Group D and Group C posts in which
direct recruitment, if any, does not exceed 75% shall be reserved for persons with
disabilities of which 1% each shall be reserved for persons suffering from (i) blindness
or low vision, (ii) hearing impairment and (iii) locomotor disability or cerebral palsy;
in the posts identified for each disability;

(ti) The computation of reservation for persons with disabilities has to be computed in
ease of Group A, B, C and D posts in identical manner viz. "computing 3% reservation
on total number of vacancies in the cadre strength". The Honble Supreme Court has
further directed to compute the number of vacancies available in all the
"establishments" and further identify the posts for disabled persons within a period ,
of three months from 08.10.2013 and implement the same without default.

Contd....

(iti)

(iv)

As regards effecting reservation, Para 15 of this Department's O.M.
No.36035/3/2004-Estt(Res) dated the 29th December, 2005 inter alia, stipulates that
all establishments shall maintain separate 100 point reservation roster registers in
the prescribed torment for determining/effecting reservation for the disabled - one
each for Group A posts filled by direct recruitment, Group B posts filled by direct
recruitment, Group C posts filled by direct recruitment, Group C posits filled by
promotion, Group D posts filled by direct recruitment and Group D posts filled by
promotion. Points 1, 34 and 67 of the roster shall be earmarked reserved for persons
with disabilities - one point each for three categories. The Head of the establishment
shall decide the categories of disabilities for which the points 1, 34 and 67 will be
reserved keeping in view all the relevant facts.

Whereas reservation policy for SCs/STs/OBCs is post based, the reservation policy
for persons with disabilities is vacancy based.

List of identified posts for the persons with disabilities issued by the Department of

Sir/Madam,

As you are aware that EPF Pensioners’ Associations and Federation have time and
again raised various issues like non-settlement of medical bills, non- fixation of pension or
pension benefits etc.

It is reiterated that we are committed to provide trouble free & efficient services to all
our ex-employees. It is very important that we accord utmost priority and take all necessary
steps to look into their issues and resolve them expeditiously.

However it has been informed by the Pensioners Association that following common
problem are being faced in many regions:-

a) Undue delay / wrong calculation of medical reimbursement for indoor treatment;

b) Long delay in settlement of Pension, Gratuity, GIS payment;

c) Non -issuance of ID Card to pensioners;

d) Non- implementation of cashless medical facility for indoor treatment by private
hospitals to retired employees and their families;

e) Delay in payment of Fixed Medical Allowance;

f) Non- reconciliation of pension payment by State Bank of India,

-2In this connection your kind attention is invited to Head Office Circular No. HRM8/12(01)2011/HQ/Pen. Asso. /21033, dated 10.01.2014 regarding appointment of Nodal Officers
to oversee the cases/grivences of EPFO Pensioners in respective offices. You are also requested
to intimate Name, Telephone No. and Address of the Nodal Officer to the Federation of All
India Pensioners Association of Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation, Head Quarter 16/3,
Safire Apts., 11" Avenue, Ashok Nagar, Chennai-600083.(Mobile No. 09381004396).

The responsibilities of the Nodal Officers are as follows:-
i) To maintain a data of EPF pensioners in the entire region;
ii) To have a six monthly meeting with the disbursing bank/PO/agencies for
reconciliation of pension;
iii) To ensure timely payment of DA/arrears etc;
iv) To redress the grievances of pensioners as per rule, within a period of 30 days;
v) To attend to all Head Office instructions regarding pensioners welfare.

OFFICE MEMORANDUM

Subject: Recovery of wrongful/excess payments made to Government servants.

The undersigned is directed to say that the issue of recovery of.
wrongful/excess payments made to Government servants has been examined in
consultation with the Department of Expenditure and the Department of Legal —
Affairs in the light of the recent judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Chandi
Prasad Uniyal And Ors vs State Of Uttarakhand And Ors, 2012 AIR SCW 4742,
(2012) 8 SCC 417, decided on 17" August, 2012. The Hon’ble Court has observed

“" ameunder: Sie

15. We are not convinced that this Court in various judgments referred to
hereinbefore has laid down any proposition of law that only if the State
or its officials establish that there was misrepresentation or fraud on the
part of the recipients of the excess pay, then only the amount paid could
be recovered..On the other hand, most of the cases referred to
hereinbefore turned on the peculiar facts and circumstances of those
cases either because the recipients had retired or on the verge of
retirement or were occupying lower posts in the administrative
hierarchy.

16. We are concerned with the excess payment of public money which is
often described as “tax payers money” which belongs neither to the
officers who have effected over-payment nor that of the recipients. We
fail to see why the concept of fraud or misrepresentation is being
brought in such situations. Question to be asked is whether excess
money has been paid or not may be due to a bona fide mistake. Possibly,
effecting excess payment of public money by Government officers may
be due to various reasons like negligence, carelessness, collusion,
favouritism etc. because money in such situation does not belong to the
payer or the payee. Situations may also arise where both the payer and
the payee are at fault, then the mistake is mutual. Payments are being
effected in many situations without any authority of law and payments

to improve the working of the EPFO. A presentation was made before your
goodself on your joining. A subsequent presentation made to your goodself

because of two main reasons; things to do are too many and methodolagy to
do them is not clear. Obviously giving time lines becomes difficult.

a roadmap and time lines for various important functions of EPFO. These
important initiatiatte, according to us, if iT implemented will, bring lot of relief for
the stakeholders.

number to members of EPFO is a long pending task. A

March, 2014. It is expected that universal number will be allotted
to the present active members by 15” October, 2014 and

/ thereafter the coverage of other members will be taken up.

\ Shas also been experienced that certain other features also
